api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.title: Class RtsNetGameMode | Panzer War Document
api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.summary: Class RtsNetGameMode Online RTS (BattleUnitOwnership.md §25, server docs/rts.md): every player picks a lineup within the budget per wave and deploys it whole; the server lays it out at one of their side's spawn points. Once all of a player's units are gone they wait out the cooldown and deploy again. Units are ordered from the map (the offline commander's RtsCommandController) or driven one at a time. The server owns the clock, the prices, the scores and the outcome. A unit's last order rides its sync state, so whoever simulates it next (the host for a player who left, the owner after a rejoin) carries it on. api/Frontend.Runtime.Impl.GameImpl.Battl.summary: Class WarZoneNetGameMode War zone network game mode: the capture zone map, except a sortie is bought rather than granted. Every price is the server's; this only shows the table it resolved. A room may let a player keep several vehicles (BattleUnitOwnership.md §16.3 A7): while alive they buy more at the usual price, each holding at its spawn point until driven. EventReference 结构，不是可拖放的 ScriptableObject。请在检视面板的事件选择器中挑选真实事件，例如 event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "list", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/Events", "fields": "Path,Guid/Data1,Guid/Data2,Guid/Data3,Guid/Data4", "search": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "count": 5 }, "expect": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)" }, "capture": { "Data1": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 1, "as": "int" }, "Data2": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 2, "as": "int" }, "Data3": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 3, "as": "int" }, "Data4": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 4, "as": "int" } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/EventFromPath", "args": [ "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "parameter:/engine01_cockpit/zoom" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "eventReference": { "Path": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "Guid": { "Data1": "${Data1}", "Data2": "${Data2}", "Data3": "${Data3}", "Data4": "${Data4}" } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. 参数数组 展开 playParams 并添加一个元素，填写 key = zoom、value = 0.5。PlayParm 的两个字段分别为 string 和 float，组件在播放前逐个调用 setParameterByName。本配方会先查询当前事件缓存，确认示例事件存在并定义了 zoom；换用其他事件时，应填写该事件实际拥有的参数名。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "playParams": [ { "key": "zoom", "value": 0.5 } ] } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/playParams/0/key" }, "expect": { "contains": "zoom" } } ] 4. 生命周期与距离 勾选 isCustomSoundMaxDistance，显示 customSoundMaxDistance 后填入 75；关闭覆盖时该字段隐藏。默认覆盖关闭、距离为 50。这里限制的是启用时是否开始播放，不是持续更新的声音衰减范围。 OnEnable 调用 Play。若此时相机距离超过上限，方法直接返回，靠近后不会自动重播；事件为空、音效池未准备好或音效包加载失败时也不会开始播放。禁用或销毁会取消尚未完成的等待：isStopEventOnDisable = true 时归还已有实例到池；设为 false 时走 ReleaseEvent 路径，不能据此保证声音立即停止。本例保持 true。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "isStopEventOnDisable": true, "isCustomSoundMaxDistance": true, "customSoundMaxDistance": 75 } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/customSoundMaxDistance" }, "expect": { "contains": "75" } } ] 配方验证了 prefab、事件引用和参数读回；实际音频输出、音效包加载和游戏内距离行为仍需运行时验证。

{ "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid", "value": "${editorGuid}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/fireSpread/aimTime", "value": "2" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/fireSpread/dispersion", "value": "0.35" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] } VehicleTextData 是载具配置的 ScriptableObject。本页只讲在 Unity Inspector vehicleTextData 引用。下文图片使用独立教学样例 Tutorial_VehicleTextData；在你的工程里请选择实际要制作的载具资产。 确认 AssetName 和 editorAssetGuid 属于目标载具；两者都是只读的资产标识字段，不能在此编辑。 editorAssetGuid 是 Unity 制作资产的 GUID，不是队列使用的 vehicleGuid。队列载具 ID 由 VehicleInfo.GetLoadGUID() 返回，两者含义不同，不要互相代填。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 CreateAsset 对应新建资产；inspect_set 的对象引用赋值对应拖放到引用槽。以下把新建的配置赋给独立的 VehicleData；只读字段仅查询。 [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleTextData)", "${fixture}/Tutorial_NewVehicleTextData.asset" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleData)", "${vehicleData}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } } ] 2. 设置生命值与视野 在 基础 分组下展开 基础数据（字段 PSParameter）。 在 摄像机控制 分组中找到 血量（PSParameter.Health，图中标记 1）。代码默认值为 1200，本例教学值也填 1200。 在 视野 分组中找到 观察范围（PSParameter.viewRange，图中标记 2）。允许范围是 220–5000，代码默认值为 220，本例教学值填 600。 保存资产，再重新选中该资产，确认 PSParameter.Health 与 PSParameter.viewRange 已写入目标资产，而不是其他资产。 PSParameter.Health=1200 和 PSParameter.viewRange=600 只是教学取值，不是官方平衡建议。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 路径使用真实代码字段名，不受编辑器语言影响。资产字段写入会保存；随后重新选择并读回断言。 [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health", "value": "1200" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange", "value": "600" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ] 3. 高级参数 点击对应的 移动、开火、炮塔 或 多炮塔 标签页，再按下表寻找字段；杂项 位于标签页下方。 字段 Inspector 分组与含义 显示条件与读取行为 sharedGunData 共享主炮数据（开火） 始终显示；非空时 GetTankFireParam() 返回其中的 tankFireParameter。 TFParameter 主炮参数（开火） 仅当没有 sharedGunData 时显示；此时 GetTankFireParam() 返回它。 sharedTurretData 共享炮塔数据（炮塔） 始终显示；非空时 GetTurretParam() 返回其中的 turretParameter。 MTParameter 炮塔参数（炮塔） 仅当没有 sharedTurretData 时显示；此时 GetTurretParam() 返回它。 PTCParameter 履带参数（移动） 仅在 GetGroundType() 返回 TrackController（IsTrackController() 为真）时显示。 MechParameter 机甲参数（移动） 勾选 isMech 选择机甲控制器，可设置达到最大转向所需时间、步行特效和飞行参数。 CarControllerParameter 汽车参数（移动） 旧数据字段仍可见，当前的 GetGroundType() 不读取它。轮式载具使用车轮设置指南的现行路径。 MultiFireSystemData 旧版多炮塔系统（弃用） 旧版多炮塔列表，新载具不要新增。 simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters 新版多炮塔系统 当前多炮塔配置列表，元素类型为 SimpleVehicleFireSystemParameter。 vehicleSelfExplosionParams 自爆数据（杂项） 元素类型为 VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter 的数组，按数组元素填写。 PTCParameter 的显示由 GetGroundType() 的判定顺序决定：isStationary → Stationary，MechParameter.isMech → MechController，LuaVehicleControllerParameter.isLua → Lua，ShipControllerParameter.isShip → Ship，其余情况才返回 TrackController。因此只把模型做成履带车，并不保证该字段出现。 sharedGunData 和 sharedTurretData 是共享引用：多个载具指向同一资产时，修改会影响所有引用者；没有共享引用时才分别使用 TFParameter 或 MTParameter。教学样例保留了 sharedGunData 引用，所以该样例中 TFParameter 不显示；这对只练习生命值与视野的步骤没有影响。 配置移动、开火、炮塔与自爆 履带车在 移动中设置动力、前进和倒车速度，绑定 TankWheelCollider 与 Track Data，再配置悬挂。车轮 · 履带悬挂 在 开火中选择炮弹、弹药容量、装填时间和开火音效。初速在所选炮弹资产中设置，主炮参数另有后坐比例与散布。当多辆车使用同一门炮时，可把这组参数放在共享主炮资产。 在 炮塔中设置回转范围、炮管升降速度、最大仰角和俯角。新副武器在 多炮塔页通过 simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters 设置节点和独立开火参数。维护旧载具时，参阅旧版多炮塔的模型路径和偏移。 配置游戏内自爆时，在 杂项的 vehicleSelfExplosionParams 增加一项，选择模型中的 explosionPath，再绑定 explosionParam.explosionData 对应的 SelfExplodeBullet。范围与伤害由该资源提供，触发方式由脚本决定。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 MCP 可按路径查询高级参数和显示条件，等价于定位数据。截图窗口目前不能自动选择 Odin 标签页；若新增教程需要标签页截图，应由 Codex 补该能力后再重拍。这里不改高级参数。 [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "SharedGunData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "False" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedTurretData" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTankFireParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TurretParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetGroundType", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TrackController" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PTCParameter" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MultiFireSystemData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } }, { "expect": { "contains": "(Single)" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MechParameter/timeToFullyTurn" } }, { "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean)" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/CarControllerParameter/isCar" } }, { "expect": { "regex": "Count=|\\(VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } } ] 4. 检查 确认 AssetName 和 editorAssetGuid 未变，PSParameter.Health 与 PSParameter.viewRange 已写入目标资产。 Inspector 截图只能证明字段位置与分组，不能证明运行时效果；要确认实际表现，需要在游戏内做一次检查。 如果后续需要调整高级参数，先确认上表的显示条件，再去对应分组里寻找字段。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 本配方验收资产绑定、标识和保存后的字段。教学样例没有完整可驾驶模型，未进行游戏内效果验证；截图成功不会记为运行时通过。 [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_VehicleTextData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ]

manual/en/component/fmod-play-component..title: Configure an FMOD Playback Component | Panzer War Document
manual/en/component/fmod-play-component..summary: Configure an FMOD Playback Component 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fmod-play-component --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Fmod.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This page describes FmodPlayComponent: a MonoBehaviour that plays a configured FMOD event when its GameObject is enabled. 1. Component Add FmodPlayComponent to the GameObject that should emit sound. This example saves the component in a separate Tutorial_Fmod.prefab for reuse. Place that object at the required sound origin when using it in a scene. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent" } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Event eventReference is a private [SerializeField] EventReference struct, not a draggable ScriptableObject. Choose a real event in the inspector event picker, for example event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "list", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/Events", "fields": "Path,Guid/Data1,Guid/Data2,Guid/Data3,Guid/Data4", "search": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "count": 5 }, "expect": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)" }, "capture": { "Data1": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 1, "as": "int" }, "Data2": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 2, "as": "int" }, "Data3": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 3, "as": "int" }, "Data4": { "regex": "\\n\\d+\\tevent:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)\\t(-?\\d+)", "group": 4, "as": "int" } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:FMODUnity.EventManager/EventFromPath", "args": [ "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "parameter:/engine01_cockpit/zoom" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "eventReference": { "Path": "event:/aircraft/engines/engine01/engine01_cockpit", "Guid": { "Data1": "${Data1}", "Data2": "${Data2}", "Data3": "${Data3}", "Data4": "${Data4}" } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. Parameters Expand playParams, add one entry and set key = zoom, value = 0.5. The PlayParm fields are a string and a float, passed to setParameterByName before playback. The recipe queries the current event cache to confirm that the example event exists and defines zoom. For another event, use its actual parameter names. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent", "values": { "playParams": [ { "key": "zoom", "value": 0.5 } ] } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.FmodPlayComponent)/playParams/0/key" }, "expect": { "contains": "zoom" } } ] 4. Lifetime and distance Enable isCustomSoundMaxDistance, then set the revealed customSoundMaxDistance to 75. The field is hidden while the override is off. The defaults are false and 50. This is a check before starting playback, rather than a continuously updated attenuation range. OnEnable calls Play. If the camera is too far away at that point, playback does not start or automatically resume when it gets closer. An empty event, an unavailable pool or a failed bank load also prevents playback. Disabling or destroying the component cancels pending waits. With isStopEventOnDisable = true, an existing instance is returned to the pool; false takes the ReleaseEvent path and does not guarantee immediate silence. Keep it true for this example. This page covers selecting the asset, locating fields, entering values and checking the result in the Unity Inspector. 1. Select the asset In the Project window, select the .asset whose main type is VehicleTextData. Its create menu is A Panzer War - 装甲纷争/G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具/Base - 载具配置/Vehicle Configuration - 载具配置参数. If you create a new asset, assign it to vehicleTextData on the target VehicleData. The pictures use a separate teaching sample named Tutorial_VehicleTextData; select the actual vehicle asset you are authoring in your project. Check that AssetName (shown as Default Asset Name. Do not modify it!) and editorAssetGuid (shown as Asset GUID) belong to the target vehicle. Both are read-only and cannot be edited here. editorAssetGuid is the Unity authoring-asset GUID, not the queue vehicleGuid. The queue vehicle ID comes from VehicleInfo.GetLoadGUID(). The two are different and must not be substituted for each other. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions CreateAsset is the asset-creation equivalent; assigning a live object with inspect_set is the reference-slot equivalent. The sample is assigned to a separate VehicleData. Read-only identifiers are queried only. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleTextData)", "${fixture}/Tutorial_NewVehicleTextData.asset" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleData)", "${vehicleData}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/vehicleTextData", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/AssetName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TutorialTank" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/editorAssetGuid" }, "expect": { "contains": "${editorGuid}" } } ] 2. Set HP and view range Expand PSParameter. It is under the Base BoxGroup and is labelled Player State Params. Inside PSParameter, find PSParameter.Health under the Camera Control group; it is labelled HP. The code default is 1200, and this example also uses the teaching value 1200. In the same PSParameter, find PSParameter.viewRange under the Sight group; it is labelled View Range. The allowed range is 220–5000, the code default is 220, and this example uses the teaching value 600. Save the asset, then reselect it and confirm HP and View Range were written to the target asset rather than another one. HP=1200 and viewRange=600 are teaching values only, not official balance guidance. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Paths use real code field names and remain stable across UI languages. Asset writes save the asset; reselect and read back the values to verify. [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health", "value": "1200" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange", "value": "600" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/Health" }, "expect": { "contains": "1200" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PSParameter/viewRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "600" } } ] 3. Advanced groups Select the relevant Mobility, Fire, Turret or Multi-Turret tab before locating a field below. The Misc group is below the tabs. Field Inspector group and label Visibility and read behavior sharedGunData Shared Gun Data (Fire) Always shown; when set, GetTankFireParam() returns its tankFireParameter. TFParameter Tank Fire Params (Fire) Shown only when sharedGunData is empty; GetTankFireParam() then returns it. sharedTurretData Shared Turret Data (Turret) Always shown; when set, GetTurretParam() returns its turretParameter. MTParameter Turret Params (Turret) Shown only when sharedTurretData is empty; GetTurretParam() then returns it. PTCParameter Track Params (Mobility) Shown only when GetGroundType() returns TrackController, i.e. IsTrackController() is true. MechParameter Mech Params (Mobility) Enable isMech for the mech controller. Configure turn response, walking effects, and flight. CarControllerParameter Car Params (Mobility) Older data still appears here. The current GetGroundType() ignores this field. Follow the wheel setup guide for a wheeled vehicle. MultiFireSystemData Old Multi-Turret (Deprecated) Legacy multi-turret list; do not add it to new vehicles. simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters New Multi-Turret Current multi-turret list; each element is a SimpleVehicleFireSystemParameter. vehicleSelfExplosionParams Self Explosion Params (Misc) An array of VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter; fill it element by element. PTCParameter visibility follows the order inside GetGroundType(): isStationary → Stationary, MechParameter.isMech → MechController, LuaVehicleControllerParameter.isLua → Lua, ShipControllerParameter.isShip → Ship, and only the remaining case returns TrackController. A tracked model does not by itself guarantee the field. sharedGunData and sharedTurretData are shared references: when several vehicles point to the same asset, edits affect every referencing vehicle; use TFParameter or MTParameter only when no shared reference is assigned. The teaching sample keeps a sharedGunData reference, so TFParameter is hidden there; this does not affect the HP and View Range steps above. Configure movement, firing, the turret, and self-destruction For tracks, configure power and forward and reverse speed under Mobility. Assign TankWheelCollider and Track Data before setting up the suspension. Wheels · Track suspension Under Fire, choose the shells, ammo capacity, reload time, and firing sound. Set muzzle velocity on the selected shell asset. The gun parameters control recoil scale and dispersion. Use a shared gun asset when several vehicles need the same gun settings. Under Turret, set the traverse range, barrel elevation speed, and maximum elevation and depression. For a new secondary weapon, use simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters in the multi-turret tab to bind model nodes and independent firing data. For existing vehicles, see the legacy paths and offsets. To configure an in-game self-destruct effect, add an entry under vehicleSelfExplosionParams in the miscellaneous settings. Assign the model's explosionPath and put a SelfExplodeBullet in explosionParam.explosionData. The asset provides range and damage, and the script determines when the effect fires. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions MCP paths locate advanced data and visibility conditions directly. The capture window cannot yet select Odin tabs automatically; Codex must add that capability before a tutorial needs such a capture. This group does not alter advanced settings. [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "SharedGunData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedGunData" }, "expect": { "contains": "False" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/noSharedTurretData" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTankFireParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TurretParameter" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetGroundType", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "TrackController" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/PTCParameter" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MultiFireSystemData" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/simpleVehicleFireSystemParameters" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } }, { "expect": { "contains": "(Single)" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MechParameter/timeToFullyTurn" } }, { "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean)" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/CarControllerParameter/isCar" } }, { "expect": { "regex": "Count=|\\(VehicleSelfExplosionTextParameter" }, "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleSelfExplosionParams" } } ] 4. Check Confirm AssetName and editorAssetGuid are unchanged and HP and View Range were written to the target asset. An Inspector screenshot proves only field positions and labels, not runtime behavior; confirm actual behavior with a check in game. If you later adjust advanced parameters, check the visibility conditions in the table above first, then look for the field in its group. This setting switches to ship control once the wheels lose contact and the center of gravity is submerged. Ground contact switches control back. manual/en/mod/blender-axis-fix.html.summary: Correct model axes in Blender 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run blender-axis-fix Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Use these steps when a model needs a different local rotation basis. Work on a copy. 1. Adjust the rotation and export Select the affected object in Unity's Scene view. Set the tool orientation to Local and the handle position to Pivot. Record a known hull dimension and check whether Z points forward and Y points up. Work on a copy in Blender Object Mode. Select the object whose local rotation basis needs fixing. Press R, X, -90, then Enter. Press Ctrl+A and choose Rotation. Check that the rotation values read zero after applying it. Press R, X, 90, then Enter. Choose File → Export → FBX. Use Scale 1.00, Apply Scalings → FBX Units Scale, Forward → −Z Forward, and Up → Y Up. Import the FBX into a test folder in Unity. The Blender script regenerates the teaching example. The Unity MCP recipe below imports the resulting sample FBX. blender --background --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python Tools/ManualMcp/BlenderAxisFix/build_model.py -- Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/blender-axis-fix/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${asset}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Check the model's forward and up directions In Unity, verify that the front points along +Z and the top along +Y. Compare the dimensions with the original hull, then rotate the turret and gun separately on the copy to verify their pivots. The sample puts NoseMarker at (0, 0, 1) and RoofMarker at (0, 1, 0). Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/NoseMarker/transform/position" }, "expect": { "contains": "(0.00, 0.00, 1.00)" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/RoofMarker/transform/position" }, "expect": { "contains": "(0.00, 1.00, 0.00)" } } ] For other axis issues, check the source model's local axes, FBX export options and Unity import settings. See vehicle basics for hierarchy setup.

manual/en/mod/fixed-angle-reload.html.summary: Fixed-Angle Reload Configuration 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fixed-angle-reload --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "sharedGun": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_SharedGunData.asset", "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_VehicleTextData.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar-SharedGun.asset", "${sharedGun}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicle}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } Fixed-angle reload uses the gun buff TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff. After firing or switching shell type, it can wait for a configured delay, constrain turret angles and scale rotation speeds. The constraint is removed after reloading finishes. 1. Prepare shared gun parameters In the Project window choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Shared Data - 共享数据 > Gun - 炮管 to create SharedGunData. Expand tankFireParameter and find the Buffs reference list, buffRefs. This recipe copies an existing gun configuration to preserve its initialization data. Editing shared gun data affects all referencing vehicles. For a change to one vehicle, create a separate shared-data copy, or clear that vehicle's sharedGunData before editing its own TFParameter. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter" }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } } ] 2. Add the fixed-angle reload buff Add an entry to buffRefs, choose TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff and expand its configuration. Use these teaching values: Field Teaching value and meaning hasDelay / delay Enable the delay and set it to 0.5 seconds isTraverseLocked Enable Lock Traverse hasSpecificTraverseAngle / specificTraverseAngle Enable the specific traverse angle and set 0 degrees hasSpecificElevationAngle / specificElevationAngle Enable the specific elevation angle and set 5 degrees isOverrideTraverseSpeed / overrideTraverseSpeedCoff Override traverse speed with -0.5, a 50% reduction isOverrideElevationSpeed Leave disabled to preserve elevation speed Delay, angle and speed-coefficient fields are shown when their respective switches are enabled. When no specific angle is supplied, the code uses the current angle on entering the fixed-angle state. These values illustrate configuration only. The current list is AbstractTankFireBuffCasterSafeRef[]; the legacy buffs field is deprecated. The MCP recipe creates a real SafeRef entry by supplying both its type and configuration JSON. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Whole-array JSON assignment creates real SafeRef entries with the type name and serialized configuration. The recipe verifies persisted data and leaves deprecated buffs untouched. [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs", "value": "[{\"fullName\":\"ShanghaiWindy.Core.TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff\",\"className\":\"ShanghaiWindy.Core.TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff, Core\",\"json\":\"{\\\"hasDelay\\\":true,\\\"delay\\\":0.5,\\\"isTraverseLocked\\\":true,\\\"hasSpecificTraverseAngle\\\":true,\\\"specificTraverseAngle\\\":0,\\\"hasSpecificElevationAngle\\\":true,\\\"specificElevationAngle\\\":5,\\\"isOverrideTraverseSpeed\\\":true,\\\"overrideTraverseSpeedCoff\\\":-0.5,\\\"isOverrideElevationSpeed\\\":false}\",\"safeRefAssetProvider\":{\"assets\":[]}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/fullName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"specificElevationAngle\":5" } } ] 3. Bind it to a vehicle Assign the shared gun asset to VehicleTextData.sharedGunData. When set, GetTankFireParam() reads that asset's tankFireParameter. Without a shared reference, it reads the vehicle's TFParameter. Save and read the buff configuration back to confirm the intended asset is used. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/sharedGunData", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/GetTankFireParam()/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"overrideTraverseSpeedCoff\":-0.5" } } ] 4. Check Verify the type, delay, angles, speed coefficient and shared reference. Runtime code removes the constraint through a periodic check after reloading completes. This tutorial does not verify the in-game constraint or restoration behavior. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions These calls verify editor configuration, shared references and persistence. Fixed angles, speed scaling and restoration after reload still require an in-game check. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"delay\":0.5" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/sharedGunData/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_FixedAngleReload_SharedGunData" } } ]

manual/en/mod/fmod-project-setup.html.title: Set up an FMOD project | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/fmod-project-setup.html.summary: Set up an FMOD project 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run fmod-project-setup Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "sdkCheckout": "../../../Panzer-War-Mod-SDK" }, "calls": [] } 1. Open the project and build banks Install FMOD Studio first. If you have a complete .fspro project, open it in Studio and build banks for the target platform. Check the Desktop output for Master.strings.bank. If you already have platform banks, go to step 2. To unpack PanzerWar-FMod-UGC-Project/PanzerWar-FMod-Project.fspackage from the SDK, use File → Open and choose a new directory. In the Studio 2.02.09 test, unpacking succeeded but Studio reported missing Workspace, Mixer and Master Bank data when loading. If you see this warning, use a complete project or existing banks. With Studio connected, use FMOD MCP's list_banks to check the project and build_banks to build it. The Unity MCP recipe below checks the SDK archive and an existing Desktop bank. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Exists", "args": [ "${sdkCheckout}/PanzerWar-FMod-UGC-Project/PanzerWar-FMod-Project.fspackage" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Exists", "args": [ "../Fmod/Build/Desktop/Master.strings.bank" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } } ] 2. The examples below apply to the vehicle's VehicleHitBox asset. 1. Prepare the source models Import the external armor and internal modules into Unity as separate models. Rename the mesh nodes, then assign each model to ExternalArmorModel or InternalModuleModel. The importer processes nodes with a MeshFilter. The teaching recipe creates two separate source models. Generate external armor The second segment is the integer armor thickness. Use Inter for spaced armor and React for reactive armor. Node name Armor type Thickness Plate_100 Normal 100 Plate_100_Inter Intermittent 100 Plate_100_React Reactive 100 In the damage model editor, click Generate External Armor. Move the generated armor under the corresponding parent nodes. See reactive armor for the extra settings on a reactive plate. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.VehicleHitBoxModelImport/ImportPrefab", "args": [ "${external}", "${armor}", "false" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\(String\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] 3. Generate internal modules In Transmission_120_15, the segments identify the module type, hit points and module armor in that order. Type names are case-sensitive. The importer rounds the two numeric values up to integers. Include all three segments. Click Generate Internal Armor, then move the generated modules under their corresponding parents. The numbers in the screenshot match the segments of the node name. Module type codes Code Explanation Transmission transmission Engine engine HeatSink heat sink OilTank fuel tank Traversing turret traverse mechanism Breech breech Elevator elevation mechanism Sighting sight AmmoShell ammunition rack Crew crew member InternalArmor internal armor Radiator radar (current Inspector label) AutoReloader autoloader OilPipline lubrication system SurfaceControlRope control-surface cable WingSurface wing Module naming examples Transmission_120_15: transmission part with hit point 120 and armor 15. AmmoShell_50_15: ammunition rack part with hit point 50 and armor 15. If Blender appends a duplicate suffix, names such as AmmoShell_50_15.001 and AmmoShell_50_15.002 result; The importer accepts these Blender duplicate suffixes. Crew naming format Crew members also use Crew as the module code, followed by role codes at the end; separate multiple roles with underscores: Crew_{HitPoint}_{ArmorValue}_{RoleCode} Crew_{HitPoint}_{ArmorValue}_{RoleCode1}_{RoleCode2} Write the role codes with the exact spelling and case: Crew_10_0_Commander_Gunner: crew member serving as both commander and gunner. Crew_10_0_Radioer: radio operator role. Crew_10_0_Reloader: loader role. On duplicate names Blender produces Crew_10_0_Reloader.001, Crew_10_0_Reloader.002, and similar; the suffix does not change the role. Crew role code reference Code Explanation Commander commander Driver driver Gunner gunner Radioer radio operator Reloader loader Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.VehicleHitBoxModelImport/ImportPrefab", "args": [ "${internal}", "${module}", "true" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\(String\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] 4. To give a module type a fixed value, add it to Override Module Hit Points. Other modules use the ratios below. Click Auto Assign Internal Module Hit Points in the HitBox editor. Verify the HP on the generated InternalModule components and press Ctrl+S to save. Vehicle rank 1–3 4–6 7–8 9–10 11–12 13–15 Base HP 50 100 200 300 350 380 The original guide recommends a base HP of no more than 400. The columns below give results for each example base HP. The editor multiplies by the ratio and rounds the result, so in current Unity, 50 × 0.25 becomes 12. Module types Ratio 50 100 200 300 350 380 Transmission, WheelOrTrack 0.4 20 40 80 120 140 152 Engine, MainStructure 0.8 40 80 160 240 280 304 HeatSink, Breech, Barrel, Elevator 0.25 12 25 50 75 88 95 OilTank, Traversing, AmmoShell, InternalArmor 0.5 25 50 100 150 175 190 Sighting, Radiator 0.2 10 20 40 60 70 76 Other types except Crew 1 50 100 200 300 350 380 Crew HP comes from Crew Wear Type. None uses 10, Vast uses 20, Alien uses 50, and Huawei uses 100. The example reuses a VehicleQuery every 0.5 seconds to find the nearest enemy aircraft within 3,000 metres. Online queries respect team visibility. The warning logs once when a target appears. It can fire again after the query returns no targets. Supply a valid FMOD event GUID to play a sound with the warning. Behavior() Property = { warnDistance = { type = "number", value = 3000 }, soundGuid = { type = "string", value = "" }, } local AirThreatWarning = class("AirThreatWarning") function AirThreatWarning:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) self.vehicle = vehicle self.query = VehicleAPI.CreateQuery() self.query.Kind = VehicleKind.Flight self.query.Relation = VehicleRelation.Enemy self.query.MaxDistance = self.warnDistance self.query.MaxCount = 1 self.query.SortByDistance = true self.warned = false self.script:SetUpdateInterval(0.5) end function AirThreatWarning:OnUpdated() if self.query == nil or not VehicleAPI.IsLocalPlayer(self.vehicle) then return end local count = self.query:Run(self.vehicle) if count == 0 then self.warned = false return end if self.warned then return end local nearest = self.query:Get(0) if nearest == nil then return end self.warned = true print(string.format("[AirWarning] %s at %.0f m", VehicleAPI.GetDisplayName(nearest), self.query:GetDistance(0))) if self.soundGuid ~= "" then SoundAPI.PlayOneShot(self.soundGuid, self.transform.position) end end return AirThreatWarning Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP manual/en/mod/lua-api2-charged-shot.html.summary:
Add a charge bonus to the primary weapon 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-api2-charged-shot Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/ChargedShot.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ChargedShot.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Attach the script to a vehicle. The example gives weapon index 0 a four-second charge time and a maximum 50% damage bonus. Charging starts after reload. Firing resets the charge. Use BuffAPI.CreateValueBuff to attach one mutable buff to DamageBuffedCoff. Update it with SetValue and remove it when the behaviour is destroyed. Behavior() Property = { maxBonus = { type = "number", value = 0.5 }, chargeTime = { type = "number", value = 4 }, } local ChargedShot = class("ChargedShot") function ChargedShot:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) local weapon = WeaponAPI.GetWeapon(vehicle, 0) if weapon == nil or self.chargeTime <= 0 then self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(false) return end self.weapon = weapon self.damage = weapon.DamageBuffedCoff self.charge = 0 self.buff = BuffAPI.CreateValueBuff("Charged Shot", false, 0) self.damage:AddBuff(self.buff) WeaponAPI.OnFired(self.script, weapon, function() self.charge = 0 self.buff:SetValue(0) end) self.script:SetUpdateInterval(0.1) end function ChargedShot:OnUpdated(dt) if self.buff == nil or not WeaponAPI.IsReloaded(self.weapon) then return end self.charge = math.min(self.charge + dt / self.chargeTime, 1) self.buff:SetValue(self.charge * self.maxBonus) end function ChargedShot:OnDestroyed() if self.buff ~= nil then The ground branch uses TankAPI.GetEngineState, which returns success, RPM, RPM percentage, gear, speed and reverse status. Multiply RPM by 6 to get degrees per second. Set the zero-based weaponIndex and the text to match in object names, modelPrefix. Matching is case-sensitive. The script caches the models during initialization and shows the first models in the list according to the weapon's current ammo count. An ammo change refreshes the display. When ammo decreases, the models at the end disappear first. Behavior() Property = { weaponIndex = { type = "number", value = 1 }, modelPrefix = { type = "string", value = "Missile_" }, } local MissileRack = class("MissileRack") function MissileRack:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) self.weapon = WeaponAPI.GetWeapon(vehicle, self.weaponIndex) if self.weapon == nil then return end self.models = TransformAPI.FindAllDeep(self.transform, self.modelPrefix) self:Refresh() WeaponAPI.OnAmmoChanged(self.script, self.weapon, function() self:Refresh() end) end function MissileRack:Refresh() local left = WeaponAPI.GetTotalAmmo(self.weapon) for index = 0, self.models.Length - 1 do self.models[index].gameObject:SetActive(index < left) end end return MissileRack Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-api2-missile-rack/example.lua", "${script}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${prefab}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "children": [ "Missile_1", "Missile_2" ], "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ], "values": { "instanceLuaProperty": { "numberProperties": [ { "variableName": "weaponIndex", "value": 1 } ], "stringProperties": [ { "variableName": "modelPrefix", "value": "Missile_" } ] } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${prefab}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) MissileRack" } } ] The replay checks the initial count, consumption and resupply logic. Pick callbacks and queries Handle startup in OnStarted and use OnVehicleReady to access assembled vehicle components. OnVehicleReady can also run in the garage. Use VehicleAPI.IsGarage to check the context. See vehicle initialization timing. Create and reuse a battle query with VehicleAPI.CreateQuery. Cache model nodes found by TransformAPI.FindDeep or FindAllDeep during initialization. Handle missing results according to each API signature. C# arrays and contact indices start at zero. Pass self.script to subscriptions so they end when the behaviour is destroyed. Weapons, modules, landing gear and radar expose change events. Use self.script:SetUpdateInterval(seconds) for slower updates. Use SetUpdateEnabled(false) for event-driven behaviours. Draw cached results in OnGUI. Configure the ground radar In VehicleTextData, expand groundAARadarData under AA Radar and enable hasRadar. Set the detection range, then adjust the search area and display ranges for the model. Field Meaning maxDetectionRange Maximum detection range in metres isFullRotation, fullRotationRate Full-rotation search and its rate in degrees per second searchAzimuthHalfAngle, searchElevationHalfAngle Azimuth and elevation half angles in degrees minElevationAngle, detectGroundTargets Ground clutter elevation filter and ground target detection displayRanges Selectable display ranges in metres canUsePD, pdMinDetectableSpeed Pulse-Doppler mode and its speed threshold hasIFF Friendly contact identification Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-text-data/Tutorial_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicleData}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/groundAARadarData/hasRadar", "value": "true" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/groundAARadarData/maxDetectionRange", "value": "12000" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/groundAARadarData/isFullRotation", "value": "true" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/groundAARadarData/fullRotationRate", "value": "60" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/groundAARadarData/hasRadar" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicleData}/groundAARadarData/maxDetectionRange" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single) 12000" } } ] 2. Bind the script and update the list Attach the script to the vehicle, obtain the radar in OnVehicleReady and subscribe to lock changes. The example refreshes the contact text every 0.2 seconds and draws the cached text in OnGUI. Read contacts with a zero-based index. A chaff return can have no vehicle. Behavior() Property = {} local RadarScreen = class("RadarScreen") local GUI = CS.UnityEngine.GUI local Rect = CS.UnityEngine.Rect function RadarScreen:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) local ok, radar = RadarAPI.TryGetRadar(vehicle) if not ok then self.script:SetUpdateEnabled(false) return end self.vehicle = vehicle self.radar = radar self.lines = {} self.text = "" RadarAPI.OnLockChanged(self.script, radar, function(locked, target) if locked and target ~= nil then print("[Radar] locked " .. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-random-meteors --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/RandomSpawn.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_RandomSpawn.prefab", "meteor": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Meteor.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } Add an empty GameObject to the scene and attach LuaBehaviorMono. Save the code below as RandomSpawn.lua, import it into Unity, and assign it to the component. Assign a meteor prefab to prefab in the Lua object properties. The example uses count, fieldSize, and noiseScale to control the object count, XZ range, and height variation. Start with a small number of objects. Behavior() Property = { prefab = { type = "object", value = nil }, count = { type = "number", value = 100 }, fieldSize = { type = "number", value = 100 }, noiseScale = { type = "number", value = 10 } } local RandomSpawn = class("RandomSpawn") local Mathf = CS.UnityEngine.Mathf local Vector3 = CS.UnityEngine.Vector3 local Quaternion = CS.UnityEngine.Quaternion function RandomSpawn:OnStarted() if 10) for i = 1, count do local x = math.random() * fieldSize local z = math.random() * fieldSize local y = Mathf.PerlinNoise(x / noiseScale, z / noiseScale) * fieldSize local meteor = CS.UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(self.prefab, Vector3(x, y, z), Quaternion.identity) meteor.name = "Meteor_" .. i end end return RandomSpawn Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ manual/en/mod/lua-self-dot-vs-colon.html.title: Dot and colon in Lua method calls | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/lua-self-dot-vs-colon.html.summary:
Dot and colon in Lua method calls 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-self-dot-vs-colon item:add(3) passes item as the first argument. It is equivalent to item.add(item, 3). In function item:add(n), the first parameter is implicitly named self. Use a dot for ordinary functions that receive no instance. Compare the calls in Lua local item = { total = 2 } function item:add(n) return self.total + n end assert(item:add(3) == 5) assert(item.add(item, 3) == 5) assert(math.abs(-3) == 3) With item.add(3), Lua assigns 3 to self and leaves n without an argument. To pass a method to an event, see Keep self in a Lua callback. end

assert(item:add(3) == 5)

manual/en/mod/lua-vehicle-init-timing.ht.summary:
Vehicle initialization timing 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run lua-vehicle-init-timing Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "script": "${fixture}/VehicleTiming.lua", "prefab": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleTiming.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } On Lua API 2 or later, put code that needs assembled vehicle components in OnVehicleReady. The script runs OnStarted first. If the vehicle is already assembled, OnVehicleReady follows immediately. Otherwise it runs once after assembly. Bind the script to a LuaBehaviorMono on the vehicle. Put your component setup in InitVehicleDependencies. On older clients, resolve the vehicle with TryGetTankInitSystem, then check IsLoaded or subscribe to the loaded event. The example removes its legacy subscription when the behaviour is destroyed. Behavior() Property = {} local VehicleTiming = class("VehicleTiming") function VehicleTiming:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) if vehicle == nil or self.vehicle ~= nil then return end self.vehicle = vehicle self:InitVehicleDependencies() end function VehicleTiming:InitVehicleDependencies() print("[VehicleTiming] vehicle is ready") end function VehicleTiming:OnStarted() if (GAME_API_VERSION or 1) >= 2 then return end local found, vehicle = self.script:TryGetTankInitSystem() if not found or vehicle == nil then return end if vehicle.IsLoaded then self:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) return end self.legacyVehicle = vehicle self.legacyLoaded = function() self:OnVehicleReady(vehicle) end VehicleAPI.RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent(vehicle, self.legacyLoaded) end function VehicleTiming:OnDestroyed() if self.legacyLoaded ~= nil then VehicleAPI.UnRegisterVehicleLoaedEvent(self.legacyVehicle, self.legacyLoaded) self.legacyVehicle = nil self.legacyLoaded = nil end end return VehicleTiming Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-vehicle-init-timing/example.lua", "${script}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${script}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${prefab}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "children": [], "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${prefab}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) VehicleTiming" } } ] The replay checks that API 2 skips the legacy subscription, and that the legacy path waits and unregisters. Check actual assembly timing in game. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local E = setmetatable({ Behavior = function() end, class = function() return {} end, print = function() end }, { __index = _G })
local subscriptions, removals, inits = 0, 0, 0
local callback
E.VehicleAPI = {
 RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent = function(v, cb) subscriptions = subscriptions + 1; callback = cb end,
 UnRegisterVehicleLoaedEvent = function(v, cb) assert(cb == callback); removals = removals + 1 end
}

local B = assert(loadfile('../../Docs/Manual/tutorials/lua-vehicle-init-timing/example.lua', 't', E))()
local function instance(t) return setmetatable(t, { __index = B }) end
local vehicle = { IsLoaded = false }
local script = { TryGetTankInitSystem = function() return true, vehicle end }
local init = function() inits = inits + 1 end
E.GAME_API_VERSION = 2
local current = instance({ script = script, InitVehicleDependencies = init })
current:OnStarted()
assert(subscriptions == 0 and current.vehicle == nil)
current:OnVehicleReady(vehicle)
current:OnVehicleReady(vehicle)
assert(inits == 1 and current.vehicle == vehicle)
E.GAME_API_VERSION = nil
local legacy = instance({ script = script, InitVehicleDependencies = init })
legacy:OnStarted()
assert(subscriptions == 1 and legacy.vehicle == nil)
callback()
callback()
assert(inits == 2 and legacy.vehicle == vehicle)
legacy:OnDestroyed()
assert(removals == 1)
return "Lua example passed"

The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run material-component --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "material": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Prop.mat", "settings": "${fixture}/Tutorial_MaterialSettings.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Material.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This example configures transparency in the DE project with Unity 2022.3.62f2. CoreRPMatData stores material parameters. CoreRPMatComponent supplies those parameters when the vehicle's resources load. 1. Prepare the source material Find the target Mesh Renderer in the model prefab and identify its material slot. The recipe copies an existing propeller material to Tutorial_Prop.mat and assigns it to the first slot of Tutorial_Material.prefab. For your own model, use its mesh and textures. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/Altius-U/Art/Default-FastProp.mat", "${material}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshRenderer", "values": { "m_Materials": [ {} ] }, "references": [ { "property": "m_Materials.Array.data[0]", "asset": "${material}", "type": "UnityEngine.Material" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Create the material configuration In the Project window, choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > C Config - 配置 > SRP Material Config - SRP 材质配置 to create CoreRPMatData. Expand coreRPMatParams and add an entry. Set coreRPShaderType to Transparency. Expand transparencyMatParam. Set the color's alpha to 0.35 and smoothness to 0.4. Assign the same Material asset used by the Mesh Renderer slot to linkedMaterial. For a camouflage setup, select VehicleCamouflage. The hasMask and maskTex fields in vehicleCamoflageMatParam supply the mask to the selected shader. Consult that shader for its channel meanings. Merge PBR mask channels 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run merge-texture-channels In the mod SDK's GM Editor, open Remap PBR Masks. Assign metallic, occlusion, and smoothness. If you have a roughness map, put it in the smoothness slot and enable Is Roughness. Select Create Mask Map and save a PNG. The output uses the metallic texture's dimensions, or 512 × 512 if you omit metallic. Output channel Source R Red channel of metallic G Green channel of occlusion B 0 A Red channel of smoothness, transformed by the tool. For roughness, the tool inverts the transformed value Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEngine.SystemInfo/graphicsDeviceName" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Standalone shader check in DE. It needs an adjacent Panzer-War-Mod-SDK checkout and an unused TutorialMaskTest folder. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "Assets", "TutorialMaskTest" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:System.IO.File/Copy", "args": [ "../../../Panzer-War-Mod-SDK/Packages/Sdk/com.shanghaiwindy.middlelayer/Tools/TextureMergeTool/Editor/MaskMap.shader", "Assets/TutorialMaskTest/SDKMask.shader" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "Assets/TutorialMaskTest/SDKMask.shader", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local U = CS.UnityEngine
local function texture(r, g)
 local image = U.Texture2D(2, 2, U.TextureFormat.RGBA32, false, true)
 for x = 0, 1 do
 for y = 0, 1 do
 image:SetPixel(x, y, U.Color(r, g, 0, 1))
 end
 end
 image:Apply()
 return image
end
local shader = U.Shader.Find("Hidden/MaskMap")
assert(shader and shader.isSupported, 'SDK MaskMap shader did not import')
local material = U.Material(shader)
local metal, ao, smooth = texture(0.25, 0.4), texture(0.1, 0.75), texture(0.48, 0.8)
local readout = texture(0, 0)
local target = U.RenderTexture(2, 2, 0, U.RenderTextureFormat.ARGB32, U.RenderTextureReadWrite.Linear)
local active = U.RenderTexture.active
local ok, failure = pcall(function()
 material:SetTexture("_Metallic", metal)
 material:SetTexture("_Occlusion", ao)
 material:SetTexture("_Smoothness", smooth)
 for useRoughness = 0, 1 do
 material:SetFloat("_UseRoughness", useRoughness)
 U.Graphics.Blit(metal, target, material)
 U.RenderTexture.active = target
 readout:ReadPixels(U.Rect(0, 0, 2, 2), 0, 0)
 local read = readout:GetPixel(0, 0)
 local expect = smooth:GetPixel(0, 0).r ^ 0.45
 if useRoughness == 1 then expect = 1 - expect end
 assert(math.abs(read.r - .25) < .015 and math.abs(read.g - .75) < .015 and read.b < .01)
 assert(math.abs(read.a - expect) < .015, tostring(read.a) .. ' != ' .. tostring(expect))
 end
end)
U.RenderTexture.active = active
for _, asset in ipairs({ material, metal, ao, smooth, readout, target }) do U.Object.DestroyImmediate(asset) end
assert(ok, failure)
return "SDK RGBA channels and roughness passed"
", "tutorial-mask", "null" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "SDK RGBA channels and roughness passed" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/DeleteAsset", "args": [ "Assets/TutorialMaskTest" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } } ] Use the output as the material's mask texture. manual/en/mod/mod-tools-changelog.html.summary: Mod tools changelog 中文 | English The entries describe the tools and workflows at the time of each release. To start a new project, see project setup. The older release channels were Mega and 123 Cloud Drive. The legacy in-place update instructions replaced MiddleLibLayer. For a current SDK upgrade, follow the project migration instructions on its release page. 2025.9.13 Switch to the new water system Sync the code with the latest game version Wave effects in this release required a separate water package. New water integration 2025.1.8 Test range update Editor interface and performance optimization The editor language now follows the system by default, and most screens no longer show both languages Code synced with the latest Steam version Note for this release: remember to update the com.waveharmonic.crest folder, the water plugin has been updated 2024.12.8 Improved one-click DIY export: you can now export in batches, and after modifying the source vehicle, clicking export again updates the DIY damage model and other configs to the latest vehicle data. Added a one-click display of all DIY parts, used to check whether any part has a wrong slot configuration Editor performance optimization Vehicle data comparison tool 2024.12.2 Added the Ctrl + G shortcut to open the editor tools Added target vehicles to the test range (the LuaProject path must be configured for game resources to load correctly) The mask texture merging tool has been merged into the tool list 2024.10.29 Synced the game code to the latest version, with support for the TV shell checkbox You need to copy com.waveharmonic.crest into your project folder and overwrite the UnityProject/Packages and UnityURPProject/Packages folders 2024.8.27 Fixed the wrong shell spawn point Fixed Android and iOS builds failing 2024.8.10 Added a path option to LOD. Fixed the penetration calculation in HP bar mode 2024.8.9 Synced the new post-processing logic Added parameters for some of the new post-processing effects If you enable the new LOD, you can opt individual vehicles out of it 2024.7.15 Fixed overpressure being able to damage friendly units Fixed abnormal ricochet behaviour in the shot trap area Improved the limits on TNT equivalent and explosion radius in the workshop Besides crew members, other parts can now be affected by overpressure (the Mod author has to enable it) 2024.7.14 Added support for editing the reverse track curve Added several configuration options for bot aiming points Added the shell debugging tool under Framework → GM → Shell Debugging. 2024.5.15 Added a config for whether the fuel tank catches fire Added an option for whether the observation sight can control the main gun 2024.5.2 Capture mode configuration Add capture zone config 2024.4.30 Preset Vehicle Queue Zoom Ratio 2024.4.22 We turned off r/w on the vehicle LOD files, halving their memory cost. manual/en/mod/modding-issue-archive.html.summary: Modding issue archive 中文 | English These issues and troubleshooting steps come from older versions of the tools. The screenshots show the settings and menu locations from those versions. 1. Map invisible collision Symptom: An invisible collision exists somewhere on the map, blocking objects or shell trajectories in that area. Check used at the time: Select all objects and look for a green collision box covering that area; check whether an extra Mesh Collider was duplicated, or whether the Mesh Collider was placed somewhere other than the visual model. 2. Slow suspension rebound, rolling over when turning Symptom: Suspension rebounds slowly and the vehicle tends to roll over while turning. Check used at the time: Check the Wheel Collider settings. The screenshot below was called the "default suspension configuration" in the old document and is a historical example only. 3. Map shell collision and render layers The original guide recorded its map shell collision and render layer settings in this screenshot. 4. Duplicate materials in Blender Symptom: Duplicate materials appear after duplicating objects in Blender. The original guide compared the materials produced by two duplication methods. Check the keymap and resulting materials in your own Blender version. Historical screenshot: duplicate materials after using ctrl c and ctrl v. Historical screenshot: result of duplicating an object with shift + d.

manual/en/mod/model-not-displaying.html.summary: Troubleshoot an invisible model 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run model-not-displaying --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_RenderCheck.prefab", "material": "${fixture}/Tutorial_RenderCheck.mat" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } 1. Check the material shader Select the model's material in the Project window. In the Inspector, check that its Shader supports the active render pipeline. The example reads the shader from a vehicle material and checks support on this machine. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/Altius-U/Art/Default-FastProp.mat", "${material}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${material}/shader/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "WindyVerse/Vehicle/FullPBR" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${material}/shader/isSupported" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } } ] 2. Check the Renderer and material slots Select the child object that draws the mesh. Check the enable box on its Mesh Renderer or Skinned Mesh Renderer component. Expand Materials and verify the material references. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshRenderer", "child": "Hull", "children": [ "Hull" ], "values": { "m_Enabled": true }, "references": [ { "property": "m_Materials.Array.data[0]", "asset": "${material}", "type": "UnityEngine.Material" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/Hull/GetComponent(MeshRenderer)/enabled" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/Hull/GetComponent(MeshRenderer)/sharedMaterial/shader/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "WindyVerse/Vehicle/FullPBR" } } ] 3. Check the Camera's Culling Mask Find the model object's Layer at the top of the Inspector. Select the Camera that renders the view and include that layer in its Culling Mask. The example excludes the Default layer and then adds it back. "OK:" }, "phase": "build" } ] } Build a separate .modpack for each target. The game requires AssetBundles built for the platform it runs on. Prerequisites Install the matching Unity version and platform modules. The project is registered in GameHub. If it is not, click Add Path in GameHub and point it at that Unity project. Local file: dependencies (adjacent UnityProject / Packages layout) resolve correctly, and the SDK dependency matches the build for this platform. Create the soft-linked project In GameHub, select the target platform you want to build for. GameHub creates a soft-linked project for that platform; click Copy to copy its path. Open Unity Hub, click Add project from disk, and enter the path copied in step 2. Click the version, change Current Platform to the platform of the project you created, make sure the name matches, then click Open. After the project opens, check the target in File → Build Settings and wait for import to finish. GameHub's linked projects share source assets. Each platform keeps its own Library. Follow the GameHub and Unity Hub steps manually, then use MCP to check the target of the open project. Then run Package Mod Now on the associated ModPackage. Keep the generated .modpack and its .modpack.json sidecar. Check the platform, Unity version, resource manifest and metadata, then test it in the game on that platform. After changing resources or switching platforms, repeat the first two build steps. manual/en/mod/physics-wheels.html.title: Configure a Wheeled Vehicle | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/physics-wheels.html.summary: Configure a Wheeled Vehicle 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run physics-wheels --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheeledVehicle.asset", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheeledBody.prefab", "collider": "${fixture}/Tutorial_WheelCollider.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Current vehicles use the wheeled mode of TrackController. The old guide used NPhysicCarController, Rigidbody, CenterOfMass, and NPhysic on the hull root, with WheelController and a friction preset on each wheel. These names help identify an older setup during migration. The current mode and wheel settings use PTCParameter and the collider templates below. 1. Prepare the hull and wheel nodes Start from the vehicle setup guide. Under the visual model root, create Wheels with FrontLeft, FrontRight, RearLeft, and RearRight as its children. Check the wheel origins from the side and front and make sure they are centered on their axles. In the cooked prefab, the builder creates VehicleDynamics as a sibling of Wheels. The builder uses an existing Rigidbody on the model root or creates one from the vehicle parameters. To adjust the center of gravity, open VehicleData → Edit, move the orange Center Of Gravity node, and press K in Scene view to save it. The picture shows the finished Mobility configuration. TankWheelCollider supplies the tire collider parameters and isWheelVehicle enables wheeled mode. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "create", "component": "UnityEngine.Rigidbody", "children": [ "VehicleDynamics", "Wheels/FrontLeft", "Wheels/FrontRight", "Wheels/RearLeft", "Wheels/RearRight" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_VehicleTextData.asset", "${vehicle}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/isStationary", "value": "false" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Group wheels by drive and steering Open the Mobility tab of VehicleTextData and expand PTCParameter. Assign a template prefab with a Unity WheelCollider to TankWheelCollider. The runtime wheels copy its radius, suspension and friction settings. A group can override this with steerData.wheelCollider. An empty group template falls back to the main template. Add two entries to steerableWheels. All wheels paths are resolved relative to the parent of VehicleDynamics. Group Paths isMotor isSteerable maxSteerAngle Front Wheels/FrontLeft, Wheels/FrontRight true true 28° Rear Wheels/RearLeft, Wheels/RearRight true false 0° Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/BuiltInVehicles/PatriotRadar/BuiltIn-Patriot-Radar_WheelCollider.prefab", "${collider}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/TankWheelCollider", "value": "@asset:${collider}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/steerableWheels", "value": "[{\"wheels\": [\"Wheels/FrontLeft\", \"Wheels/FrontRight\"], \"steerData\": {\"isMotor\": true, \"isSteerable\": true, \"maxSteerAngle\": 28}}, {\"wheels\": [\"Wheels/RearLeft\", \"Wheels/RearRight\"], \"steerData\": {\"isMotor\": true, \"isSteerable\": false, \"maxSteerAngle\": 0}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Enable wheeled mode Enable isWheelVehicle in the same Mobility tab. This example uses no track data, so TrackData stays empty. Keep Stationary Base off so the ordinary ground vehicle uses TrackController. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/isWheelVehicle", "value": "true" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/PTCParameter/TrackData", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 4. Save and check Save the hull and configuration, then pack again. Check that each configured path points to one axle node. Drive on flat ground in the Vehicle Playground to check tire contact, front-wheel steering, and rear-wheel alignment, then try a slope. Check model axes and steering groups if a wheel faces the wrong way. Check the group's actual collider template if the tires lose grip unexpectedly.
