into a mod. It lists the vehicles a match may offer, is read-only in game, and feeds the battle-configuration vehicle picker. Not to be confused with PresetVehicleQueueConfig, a saved per-player config, not a packed asset. 1. Create the asset Assets > Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Base - 载具配置 > Vehicle Queue - 载具队列 Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.BuiltInVehicleQueueData)", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Set Match identity and name Guid — tutorial-queue-001; a plain string, not a Unity asset GUID Vehicle Queue Type — select Match Queue Name — expand it, set Default Name to Tutorial Queue An empty Guid is generated automatically. Keep each published queue's identifier unique and stable; tutorial-queue-001 is only the pictured example. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/guid", "value": "tutorial-queue-001" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleQueueType", "value": "Match" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/queueName/defaultName", "value": "Tutorial Queue" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/vehicleQueueType" }, "expect": { "contains": "Match" } } ] 3. Add one vehicle entry In Vehicle Guids click + to add one entry, then fill its two strings: Comment = an author note, Vehicle Guid = the vehicle load identifier. The identifier is what VehicleInfo exposes: assetGuid, or the lower-cased vehicleName when assetGuid is empty. Copy it from your own driveable VehicleInfo; do not use the Unity .meta GUID or VehicleTextData.editorAssetGuid. Select that VehicleInfo asset and click Copy Asset GUID to copy the correct identifier, then paste it into Vehicle Guid. The example Comment: T-34-85 No.215 with Vehicle Guid: a922ecf1-f7ce-45f9-b0f8-86a23ec26c2c is official AAA2 content, illustrative only, and not automatically supplied to your project. The list is a set of eligible vehicles, not quantities: the item count is the entry count, and there is no spawn quantity field. How many vehicles actually appear is decided by mode settings. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions To reproduce GUID copying, setup recreates only the official T-34's name/load-ID metadata. This fixture has no model, is excluded from the pack and cannot be driven. For release, select a real driveable VehicleInfo and include its content or dependencies. Whole-list JSON assignment adds and fills entries; there is no quantity field. Pack with the vehicles The asset's Guid is its bundle name with variant vehiclequeue: <Guid>.vehiclequeue Add the asset to the mod build pipeline's Linked Objects (linkedObjects) Entries are strings, so they do not pull in the vehicles: put each referenced vehicle's content in this pack or an installed dependency Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions This builds the queue-definition teaching package and excludes the recreated VehicleInfo metadata. A successful build does not supply the T-34 model. Real use requires vehicle content or a mod dependency. Select in the battle-config picker Built-in queues appear in the current picker next to the player's own queues and are read-only in game; to change a shipped queue, edit the asset and rebuild. Lookup covers room presets, war-zone configs and built-in Match queues, so keep Match here. The asset defaults to Lobby; that list is not used by the current battle-configuration picker. A queue that shows no entries usually means the string matches no registered VehicleInfo, the vehicle is not driveable, it cannot spawn on the loaded map, or the vehicle content is missing from the pack and its dependencies. Check the identifier, dependency content and vehicle eligibility when this happens. Menu path, field names and behavior come from source and Inspector checks; the pictures are real editor captures. The shared recipe verifies the queue-definition package's Windows build, ZIP manifests and sidecar. It does not include the T-34 model and has not been installed or run in game. manual/en/mod/reactive-armor.html.title: Configure reactive armor | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/reactive-armor.html.summary: Configure reactive armor 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run reactive-armor --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "plate": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ReactivePlate.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Configure reactive armor on a HitBox in the vehicle's damage model. Reactive armor tracks spent areas near valid impact points. 1. Select the HitBox Open the damage model prefab and select the part that will use reactive armor. Confirm that it has a HitBox component. The teaching recipe creates a separate armor sample. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${plate}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.HitBox" } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Set the reactive armor fields Set Armor Type to 反应 - Reactive. In the reactive armor group, set Reactive Armor Size to 0.5 and Reactive Armor Max Protect Penetration to 200. These are the code defaults used for the example. The size is the distance from a recorded trigger point. A subsequent hit within that distance receives an armor value of 0 at that position. Unspent positions use the configured reactive armor value, with penetration resolved by the game's damage calculation. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${plate}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.HitBox", "values": { "hitBoxType": 3, "reactiveArmorSize": 0.5, "reactiveMaxProtectPenetration": 200 } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. Save and verify Save the prefab and read back the armor type and both values. The recipe verifies the saved editor settings. Check triggering, repeated hits, and repairs in game. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${plate}/HitBox/hitBoxType" }, "expect": { "contains": "ReactiveArmor" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${plate}/HitBox/reactiveArmorSize" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single) 0.5" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${plate}/HitBox/reactiveMaxProtectPenetration" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single) 200" } } ]

Choose CrewSkillBuff for crewSkillRef, then EnergyShieldSkillConfig for its crewSkill. The configuration's version must equal the current GetVersion(), which is 3. See the commander tutorial for basic setup. The teaching commander reuses Aino's valid portrait references without changing that source commander. }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/crewName/defaultName", "value": "${title}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Configure cooldown Set initialCdType = Ready and coolDownTime = 20. CustomRatio reveals customInitialCdRatio, the initially completed fraction. The skill cannot be released again while its shield is active, and cooldown advances only without an active shield. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue/crewSkill/initialCdType", "value": "Ready" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue/crewSkill/coolDownTime", "value": "20" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/SetValue", "args": [ "@asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/crewName/defaultName", "value": "${title}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Configure the shield Expand energyShieldInfo and set duration = 10, armor = 200, distance = 15 and sizeScale = (1,1,1). shieldType defaults to Box; alternatives are Sphere and the later Custom example. The image shows the final custom configuration. The position follows the turret position plus forward * distance. Box follows the turret's facing; Custom uses isCustomModelFacingForward to control this. After loading, the code binds a shield armor group, assigns the configured Armor to its hitBoxes and marks them as intermittent armor. Removal unbinds that group and returns the resource. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue/crewSkill/energyShieldInfo", "value": "{\"duration\":10,\"armor\":200,\"distance\":15,\"sizeScale\":{\"x\":1,\"y\":1,\"z\":1},\"shieldType\":0}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/SetValue", "args": [ "@asset:${asset}/upgradableSkillContents/0/skills/0/crewSkillRef/displayValue" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/crewName/defaultName", "value": "${title}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 4. Configure a custom prefab and resource name This example copies the official EnergyShield.prefab to Tutorial_Shield.prefab. Preserve EnergyShieldMonoComponent on its root. Check that aabb references VehicleHitBoxAABBComponent and hitBoxes references valid shield HitBox components. Preserve those bindings and colliders when replacing the art. Missing references are not a valid shield setup. Create ManualNameBuildPiplineData. In bundleNameMaps, assign the prefab to bundleObject and use a name plus variant for bundleName, such as tutorial-shield-shared.prefab. Add this naming asset to ModPackageBuildPiplineData.linkedObjects. The current collector splits the name at dots; the example uses exactly one dot. manual/en/mod/spg-td-hydraulic-suspensio.title: Configure SPG, tank destroyer, and Strv hydraulic suspension actions | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/spg-td-hydraulic-suspensio.summary: Configure SPG, tank destroyer, and Strv hydraulic suspension actions 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run spg-td-hydraulic-suspension --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_TurretVehicle.asset", "shared": "${fixture}/Tutorial_SharedTurret.asset", "spg": "${fixture}/Tutorial_SPG.asset", "td": "${fixture}/Tutorial_TD.asset", "strv": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Hydraulic.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Choose a turret action for the main turret in VehicleTextData. This example uses separate tutorial assets to demonstrate TD, SPG, and Strv configurations and how SharedTurretData takes precedence. 1. Create the turret action assets In the Project window, choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Turret Action - 炮塔逻辑. Create TD - 反坦, SPG - 火炮, and Hydraulic - 液压 assets named Tutorial_TD, Tutorial_SPG, and Tutorial_Hydraulic. A turret parameter has one actionData slot. The TD asset enables hull steering assistance and has no extra settings. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.SPGTurretAction)", "${spg}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.TDTurretAction)", "${td}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.StrvTurretAction)", "${strv}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Set the SPG aiming parameter Select Tutorial_SPG and set maxDistance to 450. The value is used when updating the overhead camera and calculating the fallback trajectory preview duration for an unreachable target. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${spg}/maxDistance", "value": "450" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 3. Set the Strv hydraulic parameters Select Tutorial_Hydraulic. Keep the three attack-mode speed modifiers at their defaults and set the suspension and automatic control fields below. Field Value attackingSuspension 0.5 wheelElevateClamp 0.45 maxElevateAnglePerSecond 0.1 autoPidFactors (3, 0, 2.5) Unity takes the absolute value of the first three fields during asset validation and caps wheelElevateClamp at attackingSuspension. The hydraulic action requires a tracked chassis with TrackController and working road wheels. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/attackingSuspension", "value": "0.5" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/wheelElevateClamp", "value": "0.45" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/maxElevateAnglePerSecond", "value": "0.1" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${strv}/autoPidFactors", "value": "3,0,2.5" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 4. Assign the main turret action Open a copy of VehicleTextData. Clear sharedTurretData and assign Tutorial_TD to MTParameter.actionData, then switch it to Tutorial_SPG. To reuse a turret configuration, open a copy of SharedTurretData, set turretParameter.actionData to Tutorial_Hydraulic, and assign the shared asset to the vehicle's sharedTurretData. The main turret takes its parameters from the shared asset when one is assigned. The Inspector then hides the local MTParameter. Each simple fire-control system reads its own turret parameters. Save and verify the action references After saving, confirm that the local actionData still points to Tutorial_SPG. With the shared asset assigned, the effective action should be Tutorial_Hydraulic with a wheelElevateClamp of 0.45. This example verifies references and values in the editor. manual/en/mod/tank-shell-ejection-animat.title: Create a tank shell ejection animation | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/tank-shell-ejection-animat.summary: Create a tank shell ejection animation 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run tank-shell-ejection-animation --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "rig": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShellRig.fbx", "model": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShellRig.prefab", "clip": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ShellEject.anim", "script": "${fixture}/PlayAnimationComponent.lua" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } Adapted from 樱花's original tank shell ejection tutorial. Build the casing and ejection mechanism under the turret in Blender, author the clip in Unity, then bind playback to the firing event in Lua. 1. Prepare and import the model In Blender, place the casing inside the turret and parent it to the turret. The example names the casing Casing. Set the ejection mechanism's pivot at its center of rotation. If the rotation axis differs from the global axes, add an empty, orient it to the local axis, and parent the mechanism to it. The example calls this empty MechanismPivot. Export an FBX and import it into Unity. Confirm that it contains Turret/Casing and Turret/MechanismPivot, then create a prefab for the setup. The recipe builds and exports the sample using Blender in background mode. If Unity cannot find Blender, set BLENDER to its executable before starting the editor. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/ExportRig", "args": [ "${fixture}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_ShellRig.fbx" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/EnsureRigPrefab", "args": [ "${rig}", "${model}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Turret/Casing/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) Casing" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Turret/MechanismPivot/Mechanism/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "(String) Mechanism" } } ] 2. Author and assign the animation Select the prefab root in Unity's Animation window and create Tutorial_ShellEject.anim. Add three keyframes to the casing's local Position for rest, ejection and return. The example moves the casing 0.35 units on local X at 0.2 seconds and returns it to its start at 0.4 seconds. The local Rotation curves on MechanismPivot open the mechanism by 35° at 0.2 seconds and then return it to rest. Set the clip to Legacy and leave its Wrap Mode at Default. Add Animation to the root, assign the default clip and turn off Play Automatically so Lua can start it. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/WriteClip", "args": [ "${fixture}", "${model}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Turret/Casing/m_LocalPosition.x: 3 keys" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/AssignClip", "args": [ "${model}", "${clip}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_ShellEject" } } ] 3. Bind the firing event Add LuaBehaviorMono to the same root. Save this script as PlayAnimationComponent.lua and assign it to Behavior. The script registers for the first fire system after the vehicle loads. For a vehicle with multiple guns, use the index of the intended system in the fire list. Behavior() Property = {} local PlayAnimationComponent = class("PlayAnimationComponent") function PlayAnimationComponent:OnStarted() local animation = self.script:GetNativeComponent("Animation") local found, vehicle = self.script:TryGetTankInitSystem() if not animation or not found then return end VehicleAPI.RegisterVehicleLoadedEvent(vehicle, function() VehicleAPI.RegisterBulletFiredEvent(vehicle, 0, function() animation:Play() end) end) end return PlayAnimationComponent Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.ShellEjectionAuthoring/ImportBehavior", "args": [ "${fixture}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "PlayAnimationComponent.lua" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${model}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorMono", "references": [ { "property": "luaBehavior", "asset": "${script}", "type": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.Lua.LuaBehaviorScript" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 4. Save and verify Save the prefab and confirm that Animation and LuaBehaviorMono are on the same node. Check the default clip, its Legacy setting and the Lua reference. The recipe reads back the position and rotation curves. Fire the assembled vehicle in game to check the callback and playback. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${clip}/legacy" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${clip}/wrapMode" }, "expect": { "contains": "Default" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Animation/clip/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "Tutorial_ShellEject" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/Animation/playAutomatically" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) False" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "PlayAnimationComponent" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${model}/LuaBehaviorMono/luaBehavior/lua" }, "expect": { "contains": "RegisterBulletFiredEvent" } } ]

manual/en/mod/texture-channel-conversion.title: Pack and unpack ORM textures | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/texture-channel-conversion.summary:
Pack and unpack ORM textures 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run texture-channel-conversion-tools Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "texture": "${fixture}/TutorialORM.png" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } In Substance 3D Designer, connect ambient occlusion, roughness, and metallic to R, G, and B on RGBA Merge. Connect a constant white value to A for an explicit opaque alpha. Adobe RGBA Merge To edit existing ORM, use RGBA Split, then reconnect the channels to RGBA Merge in the required order. Adobe RGBA Split Export a linear data texture and disable sRGB in Unity. See PBR mask channel merging for the Panzer War Mask mapping. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions The Unity sample writes three test values and reads back the PNG. Designer connections follow Adobe's documentation. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local U = CS.UnityEngine
local source = U.Texture2D(2, 2, U.TextureFormat.RGBA32, false, true)
local color = U.Color(0.18, 0.42, 0.72, 1)
for x = 0, 1 do
 for y = 0, 1 do source:SetPixel(x, y, color) end
end
source:Apply()
local png = U.ImageConversion.EncodeToPNG(source)
CS.System.IO.File.WriteAllBytes('${texture}', png)
local copy = U.Texture2D(2, 2, U.TextureFormat.RGBA32, false, true)
assert(U.ImageConversion.LoadImage(copy, png, false))
local pixel = copy:GetPixel(0, 0)
assert(math.abs(color.r - pixel.r) < .005 and math.abs(color.g - pixel.g) < .005)

"OK:" }, "phase": "build" } ] } Start with a Blender model, then build, package, and test-drive a single-turret tracked tank named Tutorial-Tank. The tables give values you can use for a first test. The KV-2 illustrations show the same hierarchy and asset relationships on a finished vehicle. 1. Prepare the project, model, and sounds Follow Project setup to open the SDK project in the required Unity version. Resolve any compilation errors in the Console before opening the mod tools. Check the Console first if a menu is missing. Prepare a visual model and a separate damage model in Blender. You can author base-color and normal textures in tools such as Substance 3D Painter and Photoshop. Gather engine start, idle, and running audio and near and distant firing audio. For the first test, you can reference compatible FMOD configurations already in the SDK. Create a folder for this vehicle in Unity's Project window, with subfolders for models, materials, and the collision prefab. Keep your source files. When re-exporting an existing FBX, keep its path and .meta file to preserve the Unity references. 2. Organize and export the Blender model Keep one root object in Blender's Outliner. Select the child, Shift-select its parent, and use Ctrl+P → Object (Keep Transform). To separate part of a mesh, select its faces in Edit Mode and use P → Selection. Put object origins at their actual pivots so the parts rotate around their own axes in Unity. Node under the model root What to put there MainBody The hull mesh. Turret → Gun → Dym Turret, gun elevation node, and recoiling barrel. Nest all three. Place the turret origin at the turret ring and the gun origin at its elevation pivot. The barrel points forward. LeftWheel and RightWheel Empty grouping objects. Name the road wheels l_1, l_2… and r_1, r_2… and place their origins at the axles. LeftUpperWheel and RightUpperWheel Empty groups for the return rollers. Put each side's rollers in its own group, using names such as lu_1 and ru_1. The current builder orders the wheels by their front-to-back position. LeftTrack and RightTrack Static track meshes or their placeholders. You will set up moving track links and their path later. Model to scale in meters. Select the objects and choose File → Export → FBX. The original guide used Scale 1.00, Apply Scalings → FBX Units Scale, Forward → −Z Forward, and Up → Y Up. In Unity, verify +Z forward and +Y up, then measure the hull against a known dimension. See Correct model axes in Blender. Export a separate, low-poly damage model. Split plates by armor thickness, material type, and moving part. Each plate gets its own thickness in Unity and belongs under the part it moves with. Separate the internal modules too. Follow the damage-model naming conventions. For a small first vehicle, the original art budgets are a useful starting point. Aim for about 20,000 faces or fewer on the visual model, about four materials, textures at 2048 × 2048 or lower, and about 5,000 faces or fewer on the damage model. Consolidate duplicate materials and simplify hidden surfaces and collision shapes. Drag the imported FBX into a Unity scene and expand its root. This KV-2 comes from the vehicle project. Locate MainBody and Turret in the Hierarchy, then expand Turret → Gun → Dym and match the hierarchy to the parts in Scene View. KV-2 ├── MainBody ├── Turret │ └── Gun │ └── Dym ├── LeftWheel / LeftUpperWheel / LeftTrack └── RightWheel / RightUpperWheel / RightTrack 3. Set materials and physical collision in Unity Import the visual FBX, damage FBX, and textures into Project. In the visual FBX's Model tab, start with Scale Factor = 1. Keep the FBX units and hierarchy and leave Generate Colliders off. Enable Read/Write in the damage FBX's Model tab so the damage mesh can be read. Click Apply, then check that the root instance scale is 1, 1, 1 and the muzzle points along +Z. Compare the hull with a one-metre reference cube. In Project choose Create → Material and select a compatible vehicle shader. Assign the color texture to Base Map. Import the normal texture as Normal map, then assign that texture in the material. Set the hull, wheel, and track slots under Mesh Renderer → Materials. If the material appears pink, check its shader and the project's render pipeline. Expand the model in Hierarchy. Add a Box Collider to the solid hull and turret meshes, with Is Trigger off. Use Edit Collider to size each Center and Size. Check the shape from the front and side. Cover the solid hull and leave clearance above the road wheels' ground contact points. Drag the model root into the Collision folder to create a prefab. Use this prefab for MainModel later. The separate damage model supplies the penetration hitboxes. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Rebuild the tracked hierarchy with simple geometry. Check hull collision, the turret hierarchy, and forward and up before saving. [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Core.AssetBundleManager/LuaEnv/DoString", "args": [ "local U = CS.UnityEngine
local E = CS.UnityEditor
local function empty(name, parent, x, y, z)
 local obj = U.GameObject(name)

end
local function cube(name, parent, x, y, z, sx, sy, sz)
 local obj = U.GameObject.CreatePrimitive(U.PrimitiveType.Cube)
 obj.name = name
 obj.transform:SetParent(parent.transform, false)
 obj.transform.localPosition = U.Vector3(x, y, z)
 obj.transform.localScale = U.Vector3(sx, sy, sz)

end

Generate and configure the damage model Select VehicleHitBox in Project. Drag the damage FBX into External Armor Model. If you made a separate model for the internal modules, assign it to Internal Module Model. You can assign the visual prefab to Refer Model as a positioning reference. Click Create Prefab, then Open Edit Mode. Check that Unity opened the correct prefab. Click Generate External Armor to generate the plates. If you assigned an internal model, click Generate Internal Armor to generate its modules. Select a plate in Hierarchy and inspect the thickness and armor type in its HitBox component. Move the plate under HitBox/Main, HitBox/Turret, HitBox/Gun, or HitBox/Dym to match the part it moves with. See damage-model naming and import for the supported names and examples. Select a module type and preset in the editor, spawn it, and move it into position. Use the same four groups under InternalModule to attach it to the correct part. You can set each module's HP in its InternalModule component. To assign HP in bulk, set the total and any per-type overrides on VehicleHitBox, then use Auto Assign Internal Module Hit Points. Tick the roles on crew modules. To support module mode on a tracked vehicle, check for commander, driver, gunner, radio operator, and either loader or autoloader. You can leave module mode off for the first basic drive test and enable it after configuring the interior. Select the ammo rack's InternalModule. Add bounds and resize them to cover the corresponding ammo volume. Click Create Ammo Cache, or use Multi-Update Ammo Model Cache in the HitBox editor for several racks. Verify that every bound has a cached mesh. Save the prefab with Ctrl+S and leave Prefab Mode. Check that VehicleHitBox still references the generated prefab. Compare the two models in Scene View. The KV-2 visual model keeps the paint and details. The orange damage model is split into armor regions for damage and armor inspection. The two meshes are spaced apart in the illustration. Keep their origins and orientations aligned when setting up the vehicle. Configure the internal modules Open the generated damage prefab and select a mesh under InternalModule. In its InternalModule component, check Module Type, Module Armor (mm), and Hit Point (module HP). For FBX import, use the node names in the first column. For a manually placed preset, enter the values and role flags in the Inspector. The importer may have created the first bound. Check CurrentID = 1 and look for the box in Scene View. If there is no box, click Add new bound and use its Scene handles to enclose the ammo mesh. To connect a damaged module to a specific gun or turret, check Connectable Vehicle Module at the bottom of the component. The GUID identifies the system affected when the module is damaged. Save the damage prefab with Ctrl+S. Enable Is Module Ready on VehicleInfo, repack, and choose Module Based in the playground. Check that the vehicle can drive, aim, and fire. Switch to the interior view and confirm that the driver stays with the hull and the gunner follows the turret. Shoot a known module with an opposing vehicle and check its HP or damage state. Fire Near and Fire Far were fields on the old audio assets. FMOD project setup Open the bullet editor at the bottom of VehicleTextData. Create a penetrating shell named Tutorial-76mm-AP, choose warhead AP, and set Caliber = 76 mm, Velocity = 650 m/s, Penetration = 90 mm, and Damage = 100. Under Module, enter a projectile mass of 6.5 kg. This solid shot uses 0 for fuse delay and TNT equivalent. Save, reselect the asset, and check the values and references. This sample uses local gun and turret parameters. If a shared asset hides those settings, clear Shared Gun Data or Shared Turret Data first. Tab What to configure Base · PSParameter Health 600 and View Range 360 m. Leave the custom sight point off until the orientation and muzzle position pass your test. Movement · PTCParameter Use the track controller. Set mass to 30,000 kg, forward and reverse caps to 35 and 10 km/h, forward and reverse torque to 3500 and 2600, and brake torque to 5000. Fire · TFParameter Choose Standard, reload time 6 s, total ammo 30, and leave Has Slot off. Use a shot interval of 0, recoil scale 1, one AP shell, and a firing sound. Set base dispersion to 0.003. Expand Spread and enter the default settings below for 76 mm. The caliber comes from the shell asset. Turret · MTParameter Set the symmetric traverse limit to 180°, turret speed to 18°/s, and gun elevation speed to 12°/s. Enter 20° of elevation and 6° of depression as positive values. Leave direction-specific overrides empty initially. The aiming values in Spread are separate from base dispersion. The defaults for 76 mm are spread 0.35, aim time 1.92 s, movement and turret traverse coefficients 0.14 each, gun movement coefficient 0.11, after-shot coefficient 3, and damaged coefficient 2. Set up wheel colliders and moving tracks Find the template at VehicleTextData → Movement → TankWheelCollider. Open it in Prefab Mode and select the root with the Wheel Collider component. Use a scene instance alongside the visual model to compare the wheel pivots. If you edit that instance, use Overrides → Apply to save the values to the same prefab. Enter the values in the table. Expand Suspension Spring, Forward Friction, and Sideways Friction to find their child fields. Return to the vehicle and confirm that it still refers to the saved template. WheelCollider field Sample value What to check Radius / Mass 0.43 m / 320 kg Match the radius to the visible road wheel. This is the mass of one wheel. Set the vehicle mass in section 6. Center (0, 0, 0) Start with the wheel origin at its axle. For tracks, also check the suspension Y offset in TrackData. Suspension Distance / Force App Point Distance 0.2 m / 0.4 m Suspension travel and the force application distance above the resting wheel's base. Suspension Spring Spring 205000, Damper 14500, Target Position 0.5 Restoring force, resistance to oscillation, and the target position along the travel. Forward Friction Extremum Slip / Value 1 / 1, Asymptote Slip / Value 1 / 1, Stiffness 1.7 Start and brake in a straight line and check for sustained slip. Sideways Friction Extremum Slip / Value 1.2 / 1.2, Asymptote Slip / Value 1 / 1, Stiffness 4 Turn at the same speed and compare sideways slip and body roll. Leave the template's Wheel Damping Rate and Layer Overrides at their defaults to start. The track controller sets damping and collision layers at runtime. Align the pivots, radius, and track path first. Change one suspension or friction parameter at a time, repack, and compare runs on the same flat ground and gentle slope. Click Preview Track and check link orientation, corners, and spacing on both sides. Use Update Preview after changes. Orange dots mark the path nodes and the cyan line connects them into a loop. The guide is shifted slightly outward for visibility. Build, install, and test the mod In the GM Editor, open Mod Build → Create Mod Package. Use a distinct name such as Vehicle-Tutorial-Tank. Open ModPackageBuildPiplineData and drag this vehicle's VehicleInfo into Linked Objects. Verify the associated Linked Mod Package. Use File → Build Settings or Ctrl+Shift+B and switch to the target platform. Verify the active platform, then build the linked resources from the pipeline. In ModPackageData, fill in the name, description, author, and version, then click Package Now. Rebuild the linked objects and package again whenever you change platforms. Find the resulting .modpack under Build/Mod-Package/<platform>/. Check the target and follow Install mods. Use the Windows build for a Windows driving test. Check the build result for the exact file path. In the SDK you can first select VehicleData → Drive (Repack) to open the Vehicle Playground. For an exterior-only test, select Health Based. Select Tutorial Tank and check that it spawns on the ground. Switch to Module Based after you finish the interior. Use the movement controls to drive forward, reverse, and turn both ways. Release them and check that the tank slows. Watch the wheel contact and the direction and fit of the tracks. Aim away from the hull heading and check traverse and elevation. In the range, fire the first shell. It should leave the muzzle, use one round, and reload in about six seconds. Finally, check the hit feedback. If an installed package is missing from the selection list, check Player Pick, the damage mode, and the vehicle types supported by the map. If the tank spawns but will not move, check the torque and TankWheelCollider. If the muzzle moves out of place as you turn the turret, recheck the Gun → Dym hierarchy and firing point from section 7 before repacking. The old example used 2 seconds and [12.4, 10.3, 8.6, 6.8]. Verify reload at each stage. Magazine (Bat 25t-style example) Choose Advance. In Advance Fire Class, set the short reload, long reload, and rounds per magazine. The old example used 2 seconds, 33 seconds, and 4 rounds. Multiple turrets (BMD-1 and T-35) The BMD-1 example used a secondary weapon for missiles. In the T-35 example, SubTurret01 → SubGun01 → SubDym01 is under the root. The other three secondary turrets use suffixes 02, 03, and 04. Set the turret path from the model root, the gun path from its turret, and the barrel path from its gun. Check muzzle and effect offsets on each. Twin barrels (ST-II) The old hierarchy put SubTurret → SubGun → SubDym under Turret/Gun. Put the second barrel's pivot at its breech. The example used Turret/Gun/SubTurret for the turret path and SubGun and SubDym for the relative paths. Legacy multi-turret setup The old example values illustrate the controls. Tune them for your own mod after testing. For a new multi-turret vehicle, see the current fire-system fields in VehicleTextData. If the model is invisible, the gun points the wrong way, or the vehicle is missing after installation, see vehicle development troubleshooting.

manual/en/mod/vehicle-dev-qa.html.title: Troubleshoot a vehicle mod | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/vehicle-dev-qa.html.summary: Troubleshoot a vehicle mod 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run vehicle-dev-qa --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleQA.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } A vehicle fails to load Check the installation folder and platform in mod installation. Find the first error in the runtime log and confirm that the package links to the right build pipeline. If the vehicle loads but behaves incorrectly, use VehicleTextData to check vehicle data, hitboxes, tracks, shells, engine sounds and firing sounds. The old project could fail when the package and vehicle shared a name. If the vehicle's internal name is T-72, try naming the package Vehicle-T-72, rebuild, and check whether it loads. If the vehicle appears but fails to run, start from VehicleData and follow its references to the main model, damage prefab, movement data, and firing data. Compare them with a working SDK vehicle. The gun cannot elevate or depress For ordinary guns, use positive magnitudes for Elevate Angle and Depression Angle. For example, UpMaxDegree = 20 and DownMaxDegree = 8 give a range of -8° to 20°. Check the shared turret data and any directional override. maxTurretPositiveAngle and maxTurretNegativeAngle control horizontal traverse. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/vehicle-text-data/Tutorial_VehicleTextData.asset", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/sharedTurretData", "value": "null" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MTParameter/UpMaxDegree", "value": "20" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/MTParameter/DownMaxDegree", "value": "8" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam()/UpMaxDegree" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single) 20" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetTurretParam()/DownMaxDegree" }, "expect": { "contains": "(Single) 8" } } ] Handling or suspension problems Under VehicleTextData → Mobility, check vehicle mass in kilograms. The original T-72 example used 44100 kg. Check that the field is in kilograms if your source gives mass in tonnes. Open the WheelCollider prefab referenced under Mobility. Its Mass is the wheel's mass. The old example used 320 kg, Radius 0.5, Wheel Damping Rate 0.25, and Suspension Distance 0.2. The old guide suggested keeping wheel mass at or below 1000 kg as a starting point. For Suspension Spring, start with the current template's Spring 205000, Damper 14500, and Target Position 0.5. Tune after testing against the wheel size and vehicle mass. Wheel and friction setup Incorrect shading or missing surfaces Select the normal texture in Unity. Set Texture Type to Normal Map, click Apply, and assign it to the material's normal slot. Turn on Blender's Face Orientation overlay. On a closed mesh, select faces that show red from the outside and use Mesh → Normals → Recalculate Outside in Edit Mode, or flip the selected normals. For intentionally double-sided surfaces, check the material. Use the rendering guide to troubleshoot other visibility problems. A secondary turret reports an index error Check that the error in the log refers to shell data, then open the bulletData list used by each secondary turret. Verify that each list has at least one valid shell and that the selected index is smaller than the list length. Compare against the vehicle modding notes and the template vehicle.

manual/en/mod/vehicle-hatches.html.title: Vehicle Hatch Configuration Tutorial | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/vehicle-hatches.html.summary: Vehicle Hatch Configuration Tutorial 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run vehicle-hatches --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Hatch.prefab", "sourceMesh": "${fixture}/Tutorial_HatchSource.obj" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This tutorial uses a separate Tutorial_Hatch.prefab to show hatch markers, moving parts and double-sided meshes. The example contains teaching nodes and a mesh rather than a complete vehicle. Field spellings match the source. 1. Add and register the component Add VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent to the hatch object and expand hatchAttachmentSlot.attachment to edit its nested configuration. On the same object, configure VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent for runtime discovery: set attachmentSlotType to Specific and assign the hatch component to specificAttachmentMonoComponent. The project's CustomEditor adds this companion automatically; the recipe creates and saves it explicitly. Check that the companion references the current hatch component. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "hatchAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": {} } }, "children": [ "HatchCenter", "LeftHand", "RightHand", "HatchPivot", "HatchPivot/HatchMesh" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "attachmentSlotType": 1 }, "references": [ { "property": "specificAttachmentMonoComponent", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Hatch centre, hand markers and hinge hatchRadius=0.5; hatchTransform is the hatch opening centre. leftHandSlotTransform and rightHandSlotTransform are hand placement markers, not the moving hinge or pivot. The moving pivot is each activeParts entry's activePartTransform: assign the independent moving pivot to activePartTransform with identity initial local rotation. Expected check: the hatch centre sits at the opening, hand markers are not used as hinges, and the pivot starts at identity rotation. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "hatchAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": { "hatchRadius": 0.5 } } }, "references": [ { "property": "hatchAttachmentSlot.attachment.hatchTransform", "child": "HatchCenter" }, { "property": "hatchAttachmentSlot.attachment.leftHandSlotTransform", "child": "LeftHand" }, { "property": "hatchAttachmentSlot.attachment.rightHandSlotTransform", "child": "RightHand" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. Configure movement isSemiOpen=false shows activeParts. Each entry uses axis=(1,0,0), activeAngle=90, closeAngle=0, moveSpeed=120. At runtime localRotation=Quaternion.AngleAxis(angle,axis) overwrites the local rotation; it does not add a delta. isSemiOpen is a state or display condition; setting it does not guarantee runtime code disables existing activeParts animation. Expected check: the pivot starts at identity rotation, so the result does not depend on the original orientation. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "hatchAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": { "isSemiOpen": false, "activeParts": [ { "axis": { "x": 1, "y": 0, "z": 0 }, "activeAngle": 90, "closeAngle": 0, "moveSpeed": 120 } ] } } }, "references": [ { "property": "hatchAttachmentSlot.attachment.activeParts.Array.data[0].activePartTransform", "child": "HatchPivot" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 4. Save and check Verify the component, pivots and movement values, including the runtime discovery condition. Save the prefab and read back the moving pivot reference, moveSpeed and companion type. In-game opening, crew hand placement and complete vehicle loading still require runtime verification. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent)/attachmentSlotType" }, "expect": { "contains": "Specific" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent)/hatchAttachmentSlot/attachment/activeParts/0/activePartTransform/name" }, "expect": { "contains": "HatchPivot" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent)/hatchAttachmentSlot/attachment/activeParts/0/moveSpeed" }, "expect": { "contains": "120" } } ] 5. Bake double-sided meshes when needed If an open hatch needs visible backfaces, assign the relevant MeshFilter entries to doubleSidedMeshFilters. In the vehicle attachment configuration editor, click the double-sided mesh bake button and choose an output folder under Assets. doubleSidedMeshes is generated output, not a list to fill manually. Limit this to the moving regions that need backfaces to avoid doubling the entire vehicle's triangle count. The recipe demonstrates the input and output references with a separately copied quad mesh. It calls the same baker with an explicit output folder, bypassing the interactive folder dialog. Repeated baking updates generated meshes while preserving GUIDs. Temporarily enabled source Read/Write settings are restored afterwards. This verifies mesh data and references, not the final rendered appearance. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Light/AuthoringSamples/Square.obj", "${sourceMesh}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "True" } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshFilter", "child": "HatchPivot/HatchMesh", "references": [ { "property": "m_Mesh", "asset": "${sourceMesh}", "type": "UnityEngine.Mesh" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "hatchAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": { "doubleSidedMeshFilters": [ {} ] } } }, "references": [ { "property": "hatchAttachmentSlot.attachment.doubleSidedMeshFilters.Array.data[0]", "child": "HatchPivot/HatchMesh", "component": "UnityEngine.MeshFilter" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:ShanghaiWindy.Editor.VehicleHatchMeshBaker/BakePrefab", "args": [ "${asset}", "", "${fixture}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "_DoubleSided_" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/GetComponent(ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleHatchAttachmentMonoComponent)/hatchAttachmentSlot/attachment/doubleSidedMeshes/Length" }, "expect": { "contains": "1" } } ]

The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run vehicle-light-component --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_Light.prefab" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This example configures a circular low-beam light. VehicleLightAttachment is serialized configuration data; VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent is the component attached to a GameObject. Field names keep their original C# identifiers. 1. Create the component and bind the object Create a light object in the vehicle prefab and add VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent. Expand lightAttachmentSlot, then attachment, and assign the light origin to lightTransform. This example uses a separate Tutorial_Light.prefab with a node named LightOrigin. The same object needs VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent for runtime discovery. Set attachmentSlotType to Specific and assign the light component to specificAttachmentMonoComponent. The project's CustomEditor adds this companion when drawing the light Inspector; the recipe creates and saves it explicitly. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "create", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "lightAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": {} } }, "children": [ "LightOrigin" ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "attachmentSlotType": 1 }, "references": [ { "property": "specificAttachmentMonoComponent", "child": "", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } }, { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent", "references": [ { "property": "lightAttachmentSlot.attachment.lightTransform", "child": "LightOrigin" } ] } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 2. Shape and size Set the shape to Circle. Circle and HalfCircle show radiusSize; this example uses 0.3. Rectangles use rectSize instead, and CustomShape uses customShapeRenderers; the existing Light/AuthoringSamples assets are a reference. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "lightAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": { "lightSizeType": 0, "radiusSize": 0.3 } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 3. Appearance and visibility Set lightType to LowBeam, baseColor to white, and emissionColor to HDR white with intensity 3.5 as in this example. Keep isAlwaysVisible = true and isBlinker = false, and turn off isAutoNaming. Enabling isBlinker reveals frequency and phase fields. The defaults, blinkerFrequency = 1 and blinkerStep = 0.5, are examples rather than the only working values. lensEmitters contains lens-glare sampling nodes, up to eight entries; beamOrigin specifies a separate beam origin. Leave both empty for this basic Circle setup. These fields are distinct from Unity Light components. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "prefab_edit", "arguments": { "json": { "path": "${asset}", "mode": "update", "component": "ShanghaiWindy.Core.VehicleLightAttachmentMonoComponent", "values": { "lightAttachmentSlot": { "attachment": { "lightType": 0, "baseColor": { "r": 1, "g": 1, "b": 1, "a": 1 }, "emissionColor": { "r": 3.5, "g": 3.5, "b": 3.5, "a": 1 }, "isAlwaysVisible": true, "isBlinker": false, "isAutoNaming": false } } } } }, "expect": { "equals": { "ok": true } } } ] 4. Verify Check the object binding to lightTransform, that the companion runtime components were saved, that the Circle radius and colors were written, and that lensEmitters has at most 8 entries; Inspector screenshots show field locations and values, not runtime behavior, so look at the light in game once as well. manual/en/mod/vehicle-modding-notes.html.title: Vehicle modding notes | Panzer War Document
manual/en/mod/vehicle-modding-notes.html.summary: Vehicle modding notes 中文 | English Original notes by @情绪薫. Models and pivots Check the specific asset's modification and distribution license before buying or downloading it. Place the turret pivot on the traverse axis, the Gun pivot on the elevation axis, and Dym at the barrel's intended origin. Wheel pivots belong on the axles. A turretless vehicle can keep an empty turret node for the gun hierarchy. See ground vehicle creation and axis correction. Visibility and collision If internal components are missing, check the VehicleInfo module configuration and hitbox naming. If the model is missing, check its visibility, layer, material, and camera mask. See model visibility troubleshooting. For transparent areas in the armor viewer, check normals, colliders, and armor groups. See reactive armor for those parts. If impact effects are too large, check shell caliber and effect parameters. If a mod is missing, check vehicle troubleshooting and the runtime log, then follow the error to the package platform or the asset reference. Movement and detail If the vehicle flips in the garage or pitches excessively under acceleration or braking, investigate mass, center of gravity, wheel contact, and friction. Test wheel physics in an appropriate scene. For radar rotation and similar animations, put the animated mesh under a separate pivot. Track nodes follow the road wheels and define the track path. Check gun elevation limits across headings in game. See legacy multiple turrets for existing roof and coaxial guns. See vehicle thumbnails for preview images.

manual/en/mod/vehicle-playground.html.summary: Debug a vehicle in the Vehicle Playground 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run vehicle-playground Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "debugPrefab": "../../../Panzer-War-Mod-SDK/Packages/Sdk/com.shanghaiwindy.middlelayer/Tools/RuntimeDebugger/Prefab/RuntimeDebugTool.prefab" }, "calls": [] } The playground loads mods in the Unity Editor so you can test a vehicle before installing it in the game. The project is for debugging only. Do not repackage it for distribution. Copyright belongs to WINDYVERSE PTE. LTD. 1. Launch the playground Set the Steam LuaProject path in the SDK project and save your current scene. Select the target VehicleData in Project and click Drive near the bottom of its Inspector. After changing the model, HitBox, or key data, choose Drive (Repack) and confirm. Unity builds temporary assets for the vehicle, opens the playground, and enters Play mode. To open the field directly, use Framework - 框架 → 0. Home Page → Open Test Field. You can also double-click Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.middlelayer/Tools/RuntimeDebugger/VehiclePlayground.unity, check the damage-mode setting below, and enter Play. 2. Choose module or HP damage In Edit mode, expand RuntimeDebugTool in Hierarchy and select Scripts. Find Damage Mode on Editor Mode Startup. Leave it on Module Based to test armor and damaged components. Choose Health Based when a vehicle's internal modules are still incomplete. Enter Play and choose the vehicle. Check its steering, movement, turret and gun, then check that damage affects the expected part. 3. Exit and test again Return to the Unity toolbar and click the active Play button. The old guide used Alt to release focus from Game view. Save your changes and use Drive (Repack) to test the latest build. manual/en/mod/zoom-ratio-config.html.summary: Configure Vehicle Zoom Ratios 中文 | English Run this command at the repository root to replay the examples through the local Unity MCP. The command also captures screenshots in both languages. python Docs/Manual/manual/tools/tutorials.py run zoom-ratio-config --capture Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions Prepare the teaching sample. The recipe provides ${variables}. { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_ZoomProfile.asset", "vehicle": "${fixture}/Tutorial_VehicleTextData.asset", "gun": "${fixture}/Tutorial_SharedGun.asset" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "regex": "\\(String\\) [a-f0-9]{32}" } } ] } This tutorial sets the binocular and sight zoom ratio ranges of a vehicle with a ZoomProfileData asset. Field names are kept exactly as they appear in the source. 1. Create a ZoomProfileData asset In the Project window choose Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Base - 载具配置 > Zoom - 倍率 to create a ZoomProfileData asset. Expand Zoom Name (zoomName) and set Default Name to Tutorial Zoom. This example uses separate teaching assets and leaves existing vehicle configurations untouched. Click to expand MCP actionsClick to collapse MCP actions [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateAsset", "args": [ "@static:UnityEngine.ScriptableObject/CreateInstance(ShanghaiWindy.Core.ZoomProfileData)", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/zoomName/defaultName", "value": "Tutorial Zoom" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${asset}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. Set the zoom ratio range minRatio defaults to 1.9 and maxRatio defaults to 3.5. Use positive ratios and keep minRatio less than or equal to maxRatio; this is an author constraint, with no validation here in code. The example sets minRatio = 2 and maxRatio = 8 as the low and high endpoints. At runtime these two values become the available ratio range: BaseVehiclePawn.GetZoomRatio reads minRatio and maxRatio from binocularZoomProfileData for binocular zoom and from zoomProfileData for sight zoom, and falls back to built-in ranges when the asset is null. VehicleCameraZoom then converts the ratio into a horizontal field of view and interpolates within that range. 准备教学样例。${变量} 由配方提供。 { "variables": { "asset": "${fixture}/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx" }, "calls": [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CreateFolder", "args": [ "${fixtureParent}", "${folder}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(String)" } } ] } 这组操作适用于需要重设物体局部旋转基准的模型。先复制模型，用副本做以下调整。 1. 调整旋转并导出 在 Unity 的 Scene 视图选择要排查的对象，把工具方向切为 Local，枢轴模式切为 Pivot。记录车体的已知长度，观察 Z 轴是否沿车头、Y 轴是否朝上。 在 Blender 中用模型副本，进入物体模式，选中需要修正局部旋转基准的对象。按 R、X、-90，按 Enter。 按 Ctrl+A，选择旋转（Rotation）。应用后检查对象的旋转值已经归零。 再按 R、X、90，按 Enter。选择 File → Export → FBX。设置 Scale 1.00、Apply Scalings → FBX Units Scale、Forward → −Z Forward、Up → Y Up。把导出的 FBX 导入 Unity 的测试目录。 Blender 后台脚本可重做本页示例。下方 Unity MCP 配方导入由它生成的教学 FBX。 blender --background --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python Tools/ManualMcp/BlenderAxisFix/build_model.py -- Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.coreresources/Editor/DocumentationSamples/blender-axis-fix/Tutorial_AxisCheck.fbx", "${asset}" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "(Boolean) True" } }, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/ImportAsset", "args": [ "${asset}", "ForceSynchronousImport" ] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } } ] 2. 检查模型前方和上方 在 Unity 里检查模型的前方沿 +Z，上方沿 +Y，并对照之前记录的车体长度。在副本中分别旋转炮塔和主炮，确认各自围绕正确的枢轴转动。示例的 NoseMarker 在 (0, 0, 1)，RoofMarker 在 (0, 1, 0)。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/NoseMarker/transform/position" }, "expect": { "contains": "(0.00, 0.00, 1.00)" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${asset}/RoofMarker/transform/position" }, "expect": { "contains": "(0.00, 1.00, 0.00)" } } ] 有其他轴向问题时，分别核对源模型的局部轴、FBX 导出选项和 Unity 导入设置。载具结构见 基础载具。

manual/mod/custom-shader-data.html.title: 32. Custom Shader Data 自定义着色器 | Panzer War Document
manual/mod/custom-shader-data.html.summary: 32. Custom Shader Data 自定义着色器 32. Custom Shader Data 自定义着色器 Create Data 创建数据配置 Create the custom shader data from out menu. 如图所示，创建自定义着色器数据。 \ Pick your custom material. If you do not know about Unity material system, please search about the Unity material and shader graph tutorials. 选择自定义材质。如果不了解 Unity 的材质系统，请搜索 Unity Material 以及 Shader Graph 相关教程。 Config Component 配置组件 Add CoreRPMatComponent component to your model and toggle on is component based. You need to assign the guid from custom shader data to your component. Ensure the urp and hdrp should be different guids. 为模型添加 CoreRPMatComponent 组件，勾选“基于组件数据”，并将自定义着色器数据的 GUID 分配给该组件。请注意，URP 与 HDRP 需使用不同的 GUID，且材质文件需在不同的管线下打包。 Build 打包 If the shader is only for one vehicle, you can just put the CustomShaderData with VehicleInfo to pack. If it is for public resource purpose, you should pack it separately. 如果着色器仅用于单个载具，建议直接将 CustomShaderData 与 VehicleInfo 放在一起打包。如果是作为公共资源，则建议单独打包，并填写包依赖关系。 Advance 进阶知识 The logic behind custom shader data We use the custom material on your custom shader data and copy your material properties to the material you linked on CoreRPMatComponent. The material you linked will keep the following properties (They will not be overrided by your custom material). If you want to use the following properties you should keep the same name as the following table. 此功能原理： 我们使用自定义着色器数据中指定的自定义材质，并将其材质属性（包括各种勾选项和下拉框的值）覆盖到通过 CoreRPMatComponent 关联的材质上。 CoreRPMatComponent 关联的材质会保留以下属性（这些属性不会被自定义材质覆盖）。如果希望自定义着色器使用以下属性，请确保自定义着色器中的通道名称与下表保持一致。 Channel Name 通道名称 Type 类型 Description 介绍 _BaseMap Texture2d Diffuse map 漫反射贴图 _BumpMap Texture2d Normal map 法线贴图 _MaskMap Texture2d Mask map Unity URP 的 PBR 贴图 _Smoothness float Smoothness 光滑度 _KEYWORDENABLEDIRT keyword Enable camouflage 是否启用涂装 _CamoPatternMap Texture2d Camouflage Pattern Map 涂装的样式图 _CamoPatternTiling Vector4 Camouflage Pattern Tiling 涂装的样式图的缩放比 _CamoBlackTint Color4 Color stands for camouflage pattern map back channel 黑色通道对应颜色 _CamoRedTint Color4 Color stands for camouflage pattern map red channel 红色通道对应颜色 _CamoGreenTint Color4 Color stands for camouflage pattern map green channel 绿色通道对应颜色 _CamoBlueTint Color4 Color stands for camouflage pattern map blue channel 蓝色通道对应颜色 _KEYWORD_ENABLE_CAMO_COLOR_TEX keyword Enable texture camouflage 是否启用贴图的涂装 _Lerp float (Clamp in 0-1) Lerp between camouflage 涂装颜色占比 _DirtRange float (Clamp in 0-1) Lerp between dirty 污渍占比 _DirtTex Texture2d Dirt texture 污渍贴图 _KEYWORDENABLEDIRT keyword Enable dirty 启用污渍贴图 Some Special Channel Usage 一些特殊通道的用法 _CamoPatternMap 涂装的样式图 Usage Split rgba channel and lerp with tint color 用法：提取 RGBA 通道，并使用 lerp 与 tint 颜色进行混合。 Vehicle Custom Shader 载具自定义着色器 Pick custom shader type as Custom Vehicle Option 着色器类型选择“自定义载具选项”。 Change the channel name to your name defined in shader. 将下方的通道名称更改为 Shader 中定义的名称。 How to support the dirt effect? 如何适配污渍效果？ When the _KEYWORDENABLEDIRT keyword is enabled, the vehicle's AO map is blended with _DirtTex at the strength given by _DirtRange. 当 _KEYWORDENABLEDIRT 关键词启用时，载具的 AO 贴图将与 _DirtTex 按照 _DirtRange 指定的强度进行混合。

manual/mod/destructible-object-creation..title: 40. Destructible Object Creation 可破坏物体制作 | Panzer War Document
manual/mod/destructible-object-creation..summary: 40. Destructible Object Creation 可破坏物体制作 在需要破坏的物体上，挂载 Shatter 组件。 Attach the Shatter component to the object you want to make destructible. 选择合适的参数后，点击 Fragment 进行分割。然后点击 Export Last Fragment 以保存切割后的 Mesh。 After choosing suitable parameters, click Fragment to split the object, then click Export Last Fragment to save the resulting mesh. 然后将生成的 Fragment 保存为预制体。 Then save the generated Fragment as a prefab. 在 xxx_root 上，挂载 RayFire Rigid 组件，将 Object Type 改为 Mesh Root。点击 Editor Setup。 On xxx_root, attach the RayFire Rigid component, change Object Type to Mesh Root, and then click Editor Setup. 将所有子物体的 Layer 改为 Fracture。 Change the Layer of every child object to Fracture.

manual/mod/diy-map-project-import.html.title: 28.2. DIY 地图工程导入 DIY Map Project Import | Panzer War Document
manual/mod/diy-map-project-import.html.summary: 28.2. DIY 地图工程导入 DIY Map Project Import 拉取 DIY 素材 Pull the DIY Assets 本仓库包含 DIY 地图的美术素材及配置文件。导入 Yaml 配置是必需的。 This repository contains the art assets and the configuration files for DIY maps. Importing the Yaml configuration is required. 使用 git 拉取项目 Pull the project with git： https://gitlab.waroftanks.cn/modder/ShanghaiWindyMaps 打开 URP 工程场景 Open the URP Project Scene 确保已拉取默认的模组工程，然后使用 Unity 打开 UnityURPProject 文件夹。 Make sure you have pulled the default Mod project, then open the UnityURPProject folder with Unity. 导入包 Import the Package 打开 Package Manager，导入本地的 DIY 素材包。 Open Package Manager and import the local DIY asset package. 选中这两个文件夹下的 package.json。 Select the package.json under each of these two folders. 正确安装后，素材和配置都会显示已装配至工程。 Once installed correctly, both the assets and the configuration will show as added to the project. 导入 DIY 地图的 Yaml，该文件位于游戏的 saves 文件夹下。 Import the Yaml of the DIY map, which is located in the game's saves folder. 导入后，即可对场景进行编辑与修改。可通过打包成模组场景的方式发布此地图。 After importing, you can edit and modify the scene. You can publish the map by building it as a Mod scene. 若仅修改了位置，也可以选择导出地图的 Yaml。 If you only changed positions, you can also choose to export the Yaml of the map.

manual/mod/diy-to-mod.html.title: 19. DIY-> Mod 工坊内容转模组 | Panzer War Document
manual/mod/diy-to-mod.html.summary: 19. DIY-> Mod 工坊内容转模组 我希望所有人都能创造模组，制作模组不应仅限于拥有电脑和技术的人员。因此，工坊增加了发布 mod package 的功能。与分享码不同，分享的 mod package 是只读的，无法在工坊中编辑。 I hope everyone can create Mods — making a Mod should not be something only people with a PC and technical skills can do. That is why the workshop added the ability to publish a mod package. Unlike a share code, a shared mod package is read-only and cannot be edited in the workshop. 1. Create Content - 创建内容 在工坊点击发布后，会生成对应的 zip 与 mod package 文件。 文件位于以下路径： （电脑） SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\PanzerWar-DE\dlc\PanzerWar-DE\Mods\Export Package （手机）Android\data\com.ShanghaiWindy.PanzerWarDEM\files\Mods\Export Package When clicking share button in the workshop,the game will generate zip and mod package file. The file is located at （PC）SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\PanzerWar-DE\dlc\PanzerWar-DE\Mods\Export Package （Mobile）Android\data\com.ShanghaiWindy.PanzerWarDEM\files\Mods\Export Package 2. Sharing - 分享 Mod Package Mod package 文件可分享到各种社区、QQ 群或网盘。 Mod package files can be shared through communities, QQ groups and cloud storage. Mod.io zip 文件可用于上传至 https://pw.mod.io/add Mod package 文件可作为正常模组进行安装 zip file can be uploaded to https://pw.mod.io/add Mod package can be installed as normal Mod 3. Mod.io Upload - Mod.io 上传 upload zip file and click all platforms as approved 上传 zip 文件，并将所有平台勾选为 approved 国内访问 Mod.io 需要翻墙 Accessing Mod.io from mainland China requires a VPN.

manual/mod/editor-configs.html.title: 33. Editor Configs 编辑器配置 | Panzer War Document
manual/mod/editor-configs.html.summary: 33. Editor Configs 编辑器配置 Custom Module Presets 自定义模块预设 Create module folder 创建你的模块文件夹 Create a folder and create a sub folder (named after the internal module type). Then import your fbx model. 创建一个文件夹，并创建一个子文件夹（命名为模块类型）。然后导入你的模型的 fbx 文件。 Subfolders are named after their internal module type. The following are some of the options, and you can refer to the preset files in the Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.middlesharedresources/SharedInternalDamage/Preset folder. 子文件夹的名称以模块类型命名，有如下几种选项。也可参考位于 Packages/com.shanghaiwindy.middlesharedresources/SharedInternalDamage/Preset 文件夹中的预设文件。 Fill in the path of the folder you created. It usually starts with Assets/. 填入你创建的文件夹路径，通常以 Assets/ 开头。 Use your internal modules 使用你的内构模型 Under the Vehicle HitBox Editor, click on refresh button and select the correct model type. You can use your own internal modules. 在伤害模型编辑器中，点击刷新按钮并选择正确的模块类型，即可使用你导入的内构模型。

}, { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/CopyAsset", "args": [ "expect": { "contains": "True" } } ] } 定角装填使用火控增益 TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff。开火或切换弹种后，它可按设定延迟约束炮塔角度、调整转速，并在装填完成后解除约束。 1. 准备共享火炮参数 在 Project 窗口选择 Create > A Panzer War - 装甲纷争 > G Ground Vehicle - 地面载具 > Shared Data - 共享数据 > Gun - 炮管，创建 SharedGunData。展开 tankFireParameter，找到增益引用列表 buffRefs。 本配方复制一个现有火炮配置作为教学样例，保留必要的初始化数据。共享火炮的修改会影响所有引用它的载具；只调整一辆载具时，先创建独立的共享数据副本，或清除该载具的 sharedGunData 后编辑自己的 TFParameter。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.Selection/activeObject", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter" }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireParameter" } } ] 2. 添加定角装填增益 在 buffRefs 新增一条，选择 TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff。展开其配置，按下表设置教学值： 字段 教学值与含义 hasDelay / delay 勾选启用延迟，填写 0.5 秒 isTraverseLocked 勾选锁定水平旋转 hasSpecificTraverseAngle / specificTraverseAngle 启用特定水平角度，填写 0 度 hasSpecificElevationAngle / specificElevationAngle 启用特定垂直角度，填写 5 度 isOverrideTraverseSpeed / overrideTraverseSpeedCoff 覆盖水平旋转速度，系数填 -0.5，表示降低 50% isOverrideElevationSpeed 本例关闭，保持原垂直旋转速度 延迟、角度和速度系数字段分别受对应开关控制。未指定角度时，代码使用进入定角状态时的当前角度。上面的数值只用于演示。 当前列表是 AbstractTankFireBuffCasterSafeRef[]，旧的 buffs 字段已弃用。MCP 配方会同时写入真实类型和配置 JSON，创建安全引用元素。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 数组 JSON 赋值创建真实 SafeRef，类型名与序列化配置一起写入。本配方验证保存内容；不修改弃用的 buffs。 [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs", "value": "[{\"fullName\":\"ShanghaiWindy.Core.TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff\",\"className\":\"ShanghaiWindy.Core.TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff, Core\",\"json\":\"{\\\"hasDelay\\\":true,\\\"delay\\\":0.5,\\\"isTraverseLocked\\\":true,\\\"hasSpecificTraverseAngle\\\":true,\\\"specificTraverseAngle\\\":0,\\\"hasSpecificElevationAngle\\\":true,\\\"specificElevationAngle\\\":5,\\\"isOverrideTraverseSpeed\\\":true,\\\"overrideTraverseSpeedCoff\\\":-0.5,\\\"isOverrideElevationSpeed\\\":false}\",\"safeRefAssetProvider\":{\"assets\":[]}}]" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/fullName" }, "expect": { "contains": "TankFireSpecificAngleReloadBuff" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${sharedGun}/tankFireParameter/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"specificElevationAngle\":5" } } ] 3. 绑定载具 把共享火炮资产赋给目标 VehicleTextData.sharedGunData。非空时，GetTankFireParam() 读取共享资产的 tankFireParameter；为空时才读取该载具的 TFParameter。 保存后读回增益配置，确认载具使用了预期资产。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 [ { "tool": "inspect_set", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/sharedGunData", "value": "@asset:${sharedGun}" }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" } }, { "tool": "inspect", "arguments": { "path": "asset:${vehicle}/GetTankFireParam()/buffRefs/0/json" }, "expect": { "contains": "\"overrideTraverseSpeedCoff\":-0.5" } } ] 4. 检查 核对类型、延迟、角度、速度系数和共享引用。运行时代码在装填完成后通过周期检查解除约束；本教程没有进入游戏验证定角过程或恢复效果。 点击展开 MCP 操作点击收起 MCP 操作 这里验证编辑器配置、共享引用及保存结果。定角、转速和装填完成后的恢复行为仍需游戏内检查。 [ { "tool": "invoke", "arguments": { "path": "static:UnityEditor.AssetDatabase/SaveAssets", "args": [] }, "expect": { "contains": "OK:" }
